Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Gentle, slow, completely controlled Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Active Flying Play: Child becomes flying object: Pretend to be bird (run with arms out) Jump off steps ("flying" down) Spin like helicopter Combines tracking interest with movement 15-20 minutes Provides vestibular/proprioceptive input Scheduled Tracking Times: Brief outdoor observation times: Morning: 5 minutes plane/bird watching Afternoon: Active flying toy play Evening: Calm observation Prevents all-day fixation Launch and Track: Child launches objects to track: Throw frisbee, track and catch Launch paper airplanes Kick ball high, track it Active participation For AVOIDERS: Distance Observation: Watch from far away: Inside looking through window Gradual approach to outdoor observation Child controls distance Builds tolerance Predictable Observation: Same time, same place:
"After breakfast: 3 minutes bird watching at kitchen window" Very predictable Brief Reduces anxiety Preparation: Before outdoor time: "We might see birds flying" Discuss what to expect Plan what to do if overwhelmed Preparation reduces anxiety Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Neck and Eye Massage: Tracking flying objects strains neck/eyes: Gentle neck massage (sides only) Gentle pressure around eyes (not on eyes) Temple massage Releases tension from looking up and tracking Duration: 5 minutes Frequency: After tracking activities Why it works: Addresses physical strain from looking up and tracking movement Upper Body Release: Looking up creates shoulder tension: Shoulder massage Gentle shoulder rolls Upper back massage 5-7 minutes For AVOIDERS: Grounding Touch: Before/after outdoor tracking: Firm pressure on shoulders (grounding) Feet pressure (anchoring)
"You are safe, I'm here" Duration: 5 minutes Why it works: Creates sense of safety for potentially overwhelming outdoor experience Calming After: After any flying tracking: Slow back massage Deep pressure Quiet environment Helps recover 7-10 minutes Manifestation 2: Following Moving Vehicles on Street Physical Redirection Technique: "Vehicle Count and Redirect" Method Allow brief vehicle watching (1-2 minutes - validates interest) Sit with child: "Let's count 5 cars, then we do something else" Count together: "1 red car...2 blue truck...3 white car...4...5...okay, done!" Before child can continue: "Car watching is finished. Now let's..." Offer related activity: "Let's play with your toy cars" Physical guidance away from window/street view Bring toy cars immediately to child Create road with tape, have functional car play
Stay engaged 5+ minutes DIY Alternative Tool: Window Traffic Chart Materials: Paper, markers, window with street view, clipboard Cost: Under $3 How to Make/Use: Create simple chart with vehicle types (cars, trucks, buses, motorcycles) Tape to window or use clipboard During designated "traffic time" (5 minutes), child makes tally marks for each vehicle type Count totals at end Makes watching purposeful and time-limited Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Adds structure and purpose, time-limited, educational (counting, categorizing) Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Vehicle Spotting Game Cost: $0-3 (paper for chart) Materials: Chart with vehicle types, colors, special vehicles How to Use: Create bingo-style card with different vehicles "Find: red car, blue truck, motorcycle, bus, delivery van" Check off when spotted First to complete card wins
Can play with family Adds game element to vehicle watching Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Structured, game with endpoint, can be social Traffic Study Project Cost: $0-5 (notebook, pencils) Materials: Notebook, pencil, timer How to Use: "How many vehicles pass in 10 minutes?" Chart by type, color, size Graph results Compare different times of day Scientific approach Makes watching educational Duration: 10 minutes observation + graphing time Why it works: Educational, purposeful, adds math/science element Toy Vehicle Street Play Cost: $10-20 (toy cars, city mat or tape) Materials: Multiple toy vehicles, road mat or tape roads, buildings How to Use: Create city with roads indoors Child controls all vehicle movement Can recreate traffic patterns seen outside Adds control and pretend play
Build traffic scenarios Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Child in control, pretend play, relates interest to functional play Vehicle Photography Project Cost: $0 (if have camera/phone) Materials: Camera or phone, window view or outdoor walk How to Use: Take photos of interesting vehicles Create photo album or collage Learn about different vehicle types Can categorize photos later Creates lasting project from interest Duration: 15 minutes photo session + project time Why it works: Active participation, creates product, extends interest creatively Vehicle Sound Matching Cost: $0-5 (online sounds or recordings) Materials: Recordings of vehicle sounds, pictures of vehicles How to Use: Match sound to vehicle type "Which makes this sound?" Listen for different vehicles outside Adds auditory discrimination Makes watching multi-sensory learning
Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Educational, adds auditory element, learning activity Alternative Stimulation (For AVOIDERS): Vehicle Picture Book Cost: $5-10 Materials: Picture book about vehicles How to Use: Look at pictures (no movement) Read about vehicle types Calm, controlled Same book repeatedly Duration: 10 minutes Why it works: No movement, predictable, calm, educational Single Toy Vehicle Cost: $3-5 Materials: One favorite toy vehicle How to Use: Child can hold, look at, play with Comfort object No tracking required Addresses interest without stimulation Duration: As needed Why it works: Portable, controllable, no demands Brief Scheduled Vehicle Time Cost: $0 Materials: Window view, timer How to Use: "After lunch: 3 minutes vehicle watching" Timer shows when done Same time daily Very predictable
Duration: 3 minutes Why it works: Extremely structured, predictable, brief Distance Viewing Cost: $0 Materials: Window view from across room How to Use: Watch vehicles from far away (less stimulating) Can gradually move closer Child controls distance Duration: 5 minutes Why it works: Less intense from distance, child controls Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Active Vehicle Play: After watching: Play with toy vehicles (pushing, racing) Create traffic scenarios Build roads and cities Transitions from passive to active Movement Integration: Pretend to be vehicles: "Drive" around house making motor sounds Jump for "speed bumps" Provides vestibular/proprioceptive input 15-20 minutes Scheduled Watching: Brief window time: Morning: 5 minutes traffic watching Then: active toy vehicle play 15 minutes Prevents prolonged fixation For AVOIDERS:
Gradual Exposure: Week 1: Look at vehicle pictures only Week 2: Watch vehicles from across room (30 seconds) Week 3: Move closer (1 minute) Week 4: At window briefly (2 minutes) Very gradual Predictable Schedule: Same time, same duration: "After breakfast: 2 minutes at window" Extreme predictability Reduces anxiety Preparation: Before outdoor time: "We'll see cars driving" Discuss what to expect Plan coping strategies Reduces overwhelm Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Neck and Shoulder Release: Tracking vehicles creates neck tension: Massage neck (sides only) Shoulder massage Gentle neck rotations Releases tension from tracking Duration: 5-7 minutes Frequency: After vehicle watching Why it works: Addresses physical tension from visual tracking Vestibular Calming: After tracking movement: Gentle pressure on temples Base of skull pressure
Calms visual tracking system 5 minutes For AVOIDERS: Grounding Before Exposure: Before vehicle watching: Firm pressure on shoulders Grounding touch on feet Deep breathing together Duration: 5 minutes Why it works: Prepares nervous system Recovery After: After vehicle exposure: Slow back massage Deep pressure Quiet space Helps nervous system recover 7-10 minutes Manifestation 3: Watching Leaves Blow in Wind Physical Redirection Technique: "Nature Watch Transition" Method Allow brief leaf watching (1-2 minutes) Join child: "The wind is making the leaves dance!" After observation: "Let's collect some leaves to look at closer" Go outside together (if possible) to collect leaves Or: "Let's make leaves dance inside!" (fan + paper leaves) Transition to hands-on nature activity Offer choice: "Leaf rubbing or leaf collage?"
Stay engaged with activity 10+ minutes DIY Alternative Tool: Indoor Wind and Leaf Station Materials: Fan, paper or fabric leaves, string, tape Cost: Under $5 How to Make: Cut leaf shapes from colored paper or fabric Hang some from string (mobile style) Scatter others on floor Child turns on fan, watches leaves blow/move Can adjust fan speed Creates controlled "wind" environment Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Child controls wind intensity, indoor/safe, can repeat Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Leaf Collection and Play Cost: $0-5 (bags for collecting) Materials: Bags, outdoor space How to Use: Collect fallen leaves (active searching) Jump in leaf piles Throw leaves in air, watch them fall Sort by size, color, shape Make leaf art/rubbings Active participation with leaves
Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Active, outdoor, gross motor, combines observation with play Kite Flying Cost: $10-20 (kite) Materials: Kite, windy day, open space How to Use: Child flies kite Controls movement in wind Tracks kite flying Feels wind pulling Active participation Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Child creates wind-based movement, active, outdoor Pinwheel Garden Cost: $5-15 (multiple pinwheels) Materials: 5-10 pinwheels, outdoor planting area How to Use: Plant pinwheels outside Different colors, sizes Watch them spin in wind Can check throughout day Blow on them too Duration: Brief checks multiple times daily Why it works: Ongoing project, similar to leaves but more controlled Wind Chime Creation Cost: $5-10 (materials) Materials: Sticks, string, found objects (shells, metal pieces) How to Make:
Create wind chime together Hang outside Wind moves chime (visual + auditory) How to Use: Check on chime throughout day Listen and watch Makes wind tangible Duration: 30 minutes creation + ongoing Why it works: Child creates project, multi-sensory Bubble Blowing in Wind Cost: $3-5 (bubbles) Materials: Bubble solution, windy day How to Use: Blow bubbles outside Wind carries them Chase and pop bubbles Watch unpredictable paths Active participation Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Active, child creates bubbles, movement in wind Alternative Stimulation (For AVOIDERS): Leaf Pictures/Books Cost: $5-10 Materials: Nature books with leaf pictures How to Use: Look at still images No movement Read about leaves, trees Calm, educational Duration: 10 minutes Why it works: No movement, predictable, calm
Single Leaf Observation Cost: $0 Materials: One leaf, magnifying glass How to Use: Look at one leaf closely (not moving) Examine details Very focused, calm No wind movement Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Still observation, detailed, calm Indoor Plant Observation Cost: $5-10 (small plant) Materials: Small houseplant How to Use: Child's plant to care for Watch it grow (slow change) No wind movement indoors Calm, controlled Duration: Brief daily observations Why it works: Indoor, controlled, slow change Leaf Mobile (Gentle) Cost: $5-8 Materials: Gentle mobile with leaf shapes How to Use: Hang in room Moves very gently with air Predictable, slow Always available Duration: As desired Why it works: Very gentle, predictable, calming Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Active Outdoor Play:
After leaf watching: Run and jump in leaves Collect leaves actively Create leaf pile to jump in Provides gross motor input 20-30 minutes Wind Exploration: Feel wind on body: Stand in wind Feel it blow hair, clothes Spin to create own wind Tactile + vestibular input 15-20 minutes Nature Integration: Scheduled nature observation: Morning: 5 minutes leaf watching Afternoon: Outdoor active play Evening: Calm nature time Structured schedule For AVOIDERS: Indoor First: Start with indoor calm nature: Look at plant (no wind) Read nature books Gradually introduce outdoor time Very gradual Predictable Nature Time: Same spot, same time: "After breakfast: 3 minutes at window watching tree" Very predictable Reduces anxiety Supported Outdoor Time: Parent stays close: Hold hands outside Short duration initially
Can return inside anytime Builds confidence Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Full Body Wind Simulation: Provide "wind" sensation through touch: Light, quick strokes on arms (like wind) Gentle brushing on legs Simulates wind on skin Some children find this organizing Duration: 5 minutes Frequency: After outdoor time or instead of prolonged watching Why it works: Provides tactile "wind" sensation in controlled way Calming After Outdoor: After windy outdoor play: Firm organizing massage Helps transition indoors Calms excitement 7-10 minutes For AVOIDERS: Preparation for Outdoor: Before going outside: Firm, grounding massage Shoulders, feet "You're safe, we'll stay together" Duration: 5-7 minutes Why it works: Prepares for potentially overwhelming outdoor experience Recovery After Wind Exposure: After being in wind: Slow, deep massage Wrap in blanket
Quiet space Helps recover 10 minutes Manifestation 4: Tracking Bubbles Floating Physical Redirection Technique: "Bubble Play Expansion" Method Allow bubble watching/tracking (this is naturally time-limited as bubbles pop) After 5-10 minutes: "Last five bubbles, then we try something new" Count together as bubbles float and pop Before more bubbles: "Bubble watching is changing. Now let's..." Offer alternative: "Let's catch bubbles" or "Let's make giant bubbles" Transition to more active bubble engagement Or different activity: "Bubbles are resting. Let's play with this" Stay engaged 10+ minutes DIY Alternative Tool: Bubble Sensory Bottle Materials: Clear plastic bottle, water, clear dish soap, glycerin, food coloring, glitter Cost: Under $5 How to Make: Fill bottle 3/4 with water Add 1/4 cup clear dish soap Add 1 tablespoon glycerin (slows bubbles)
Add drop of food coloring Add glitter Seal tightly Child shakes, watches bubbles form and float inside Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Contained bubble observation, portable, reusable Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Active Bubble Chase Cost: $3-5 (bubble solution) Materials: Bubble solution, bubble wand or machine How to Use: Blow bubbles (or use machine) Child chases and pops them Count how many popped Jump to pop high bubbles Combines tracking with active movement Outdoor activity Duration: 20-30 minutes Why it works: Active participation, gross motor, child engaged not just watching Giant Bubble Making Cost: $10-15 (giant bubble wands) or DIY $5 Materials: Giant bubble wand or DIY (string between two sticks), giant bubble solution DIY Solution: 6 cups water + 1/2 cup dish soap + 1/2 cup corn syrup
How to Use: Create huge bubbles Watch them float Very engaging and exciting Can try to catch in bubble Outdoor activity Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Dramatic, child creates bubbles, amazing visual effect Bubble Art Project Cost: $3-5 (food coloring, paper) Materials: Bubble solution, food coloring, paper, straws How to Use: Add food coloring to bubble solution Blow bubbles onto paper Bubbles pop, leave colored circles Creates art from bubbles Functional creative output Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Creative, produces art, purposeful bubble activity Bubble Relay Race Cost: $3-5 (bubbles, straws) Materials: Bubble solution, straws for each player How to Use: Blow bubble, keep it floating by blowing Race bubble across finish line Family game Active, social Duration: 20-30 minutes
Why it works: Game structure, social, active participation Bubble Science Experiments Cost: $5-10 (various solutions) Materials: Different bubble solutions, measuring tools How to Use: Test different solutions: which makes biggest bubbles? Which last longest? Measure bubble size Graph results Educational approach Duration: 45-60 minutes Why it works: Makes bubble interest scientific, educational, purposeful Alternative Stimulation (For AVOIDERS): Bubble Pictures/Videos Cost: $0-10 (book or videos) Materials: Pictures of bubbles or gentle bubble videos How to Use: Look at still images (no movement) Or very calm bubble videos (can pause) Controllable Addresses interest without direct exposure Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: No actual bubbles (less overwhelming), controllable Contained Bubble Bottle Cost: $3-5 Materials: Bubble sensory bottle (described above) How to Use: Child controls when to shake
Bubbles contained in bottle Can't pop or fly away Predictable Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Contained, predictable, child controls One Bubble at a Time Cost: $3 (bubble solution) Materials: Bubble solution, wand How to Use: Blow ONE bubble slowly Watch it float gently Let it pop naturally Wait, then one more Very controlled pace Duration: 5 minutes Why it works: Slow, controlled, not overwhelming Distance Bubble Watching Cost: $3 (bubbles) Materials: Bubble solution How to Use: Parent blows bubbles at distance (10+ feet) Child watches from safe distance Gradually can move closer Child controls proximity Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Distance reduces overwhelm, child controls Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Bubble Chase Circuit: Active bubble play: Blow bubbles
Chase and pop (running, jumping) Blow more bubbles Provides gross motor input 20-30 minutes Blow and Track: Child blows bubbles: Provides oral motor input (organizing) Then tracks bubbles they created Control over bubble creation 15-20 minutes Scheduled Bubble Time: Designated times: Morning: 10 minutes active bubble play Evening: 5 minutes calm bubble observation Prevents all-day seeking For AVOIDERS: Gradual Bubble Introduction: Week 1: Look at bubble pictures Week 2: Watch parent blow 1 bubble from distance Week 3: Move closer to bubble activity Week 4: Touch bubble wand (not blowing yet) Very gradual Predictable Bubble Time: Same time, same place: "After snack: 5 minutes bubble time outside" Same duration, same location Extreme predictability Child Controls Pace: Child decides: How many bubbles
How close to get When to stop Complete control Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Oral Motor Preparation: If child blowing bubbles (provides oral input): Gentle face massage Cheek massage Around mouth (not on lips) Prepares oral motor system Duration: 3-5 minutes Before bubble blowing Why it works: Prepares oral muscles, some children find oral input very regulating Calming After Active Play: After bubble chasing: Full body massage Helps calm from excitement Organizes after vigorous movement 7-10 minutes For AVOIDERS: Grounding Before Bubbles: If bubbles are overwhelming: Firm pressure massage Grounding touch "You're safe" Duration: 5 minutes Before bubble exposure Why it works: Prepares nervous system Recovery After: After bubble exposure: Slow, calming massage Deep pressure Quiet space 7-10 minutes Helps recover Manifestation 5: Following Ball Bouncing
Physical Redirection Technique: "Bounce and Play" Method Allow ball bouncing/watching (naturally engaging activity) After 5-10 bounces: "Last 3 bounces, then we play catch" Count bounces together: "1...2...3" Immediately transition: "Now let's roll the ball" or "Let's throw and catch" Engage in interactive ball play If fixated on watching: "Let's bounce it together, you and me" Make ball play interactive, not passive watching Stay engaged 10+ minutes DIY Alternative Tool: Bounce Prediction Board Materials: Ball, paper targets on floor, tape, marker Cost: Under $5 How to Make: Create target circles on floor with tape (numbered 1-5) Child bounces ball Predicts which target it will bounce to Marks predictions Makes bouncing purposeful game Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Adds prediction/cognitive element, game structure, purposeful
Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Ball Bounce Catch Game Cost: $5-10 (various balls) Materials: Different types of balls (basketball, tennis, bouncy) How to Use: Bounce ball to partner Catch after bounce Count consecutive catches Try different balls (bounce differently) Social, active Duration: 20-30 minutes Why it works: Interactive, gross motor, social option Bounce Obstacle Course Cost: $0-5 (household items) Materials: Ball, obstacles (boxes, cones, pillows) How to Use: Create course with obstacles Bounce ball through course Can't touch obstacles Time trials Problem-solving + ball play Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Adds complexity, problem-solving, purposeful Basketball/Wall Ball Cost: $10-20 (small hoop) or $0 (wall) Materials: Basketball hoop or wall, ball How to Use: Shoot baskets (bounce then shoot) Or throw ball against wall, catch on bounce
Count successful catches/baskets Skill-building Duration: 20-30 minutes Why it works: Sport skill, purposeful, can track progress Bounce Height Experiment Cost: $5-10 (various balls) Materials: Different balls, measuring tape, wall with markings How to Use: Drop each ball from same height Measure how high it bounces Graph results Test on different surfaces Scientific approach Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Educational, purpose-driven, scientific method Rhythm Bounce Cost: $5 (ball) Materials: Ball, music or metronome How to Use: Bounce ball to rhythm/beat Fast music = fast bounces Slow music = slow bounces Adds auditory + motor planning Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Multi-sensory, rhythm/timing skill Alternative Stimulation (For AVOIDERS): Slow Roll Instead of Bounce Cost: $5 (ball) Materials: Ball How to Use:
Roll ball slowly (no bouncing) Predictable path Less stimulating than bounce Can catch easily Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Gentler, more predictable than bouncing Stationary Ball Play Cost: $5 (ball) Materials: Ball How to Use: Hold ball, pass it hand to hand No bouncing or throwing Very calm, controlled Can squeeze, roll on body Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: No unpredictable movement Guided Bounce Cost: $5 (ball) Materials: Ball, adult support How to Use: Adult and child hold ball together Bounce together Adult controls height/speed Child feels supported Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Co-regulation, controlled, supported Picture of Ball Bouncing Cost: $0-2 Materials: Pictures showing ball bounce sequence How to Use: Look at still images Discuss bouncing No actual bouncing
Duration: 5 minutes Why it works: Addresses interest without stimulation Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Active Ball Play Circuit: Variety of ball activities: Bounce 10 times Throw against wall 10 times Roll through legs 10 times Basketball shots 10 times Prevents fixation on just watching bounce 20-30 minutes Heavy Ball Work: Use weighted or medicine ball: Heavier ball provides more input Bounce, throw, carry More organizing than light ball 15-20 minutes Interactive Ball Games: Always include partner: Bounce to each other Never solo bouncing and watching Social engagement prevents fixation 20-30 minutes For AVOIDERS: Predictable Ball Play: Same ball, same activity: "After lunch: 5 minutes rolling red ball" No bouncing initially Very predictable Reduces anxiety Gradual Bounce Introduction: Week 1: Hold ball only
Week 2: Roll ball Week 3: Very gentle, low bounce (1 inch) Week 4: Slightly higher bounce Very gradual increase Distance Control: Watch bouncing from distance: Start 10+ feet away Gradually move closer Child controls proximity Builds tolerance Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Arm and Hand Preparation: Before ball play: Massage arms (used in bouncing/catching) Hand massage Wrist rotations Prepares muscles Duration: 5 minutes per arm Why it works: Prepares for motor activity, may reduce need for repetitive bouncing by providing input first Shoulder and Upper Body: After ball play: Shoulder massage (throwing uses shoulders) Upper back massage Releases tension 7-10 minutes For AVOIDERS: Grounding Before Ball Play: If ball play is anxiety-inducing: Firm pressure on shoulders and hands Grounding touch "You can do this, I'm helping"
Duration: 5 minutes Why it works: Prepares for motor challenge Calming After: After ball activity: Slow, calming full body massage Deep pressure Helps transition 7-10 minutes Manifestation 6: Watching Snow or Rain Fall Physical Redirection Technique: "Weather Watch Transition" Method Allow brief weather watching (1-3 minutes - validates interest) Join child: "The snow is falling so gently!" After observation: "Let's collect some to look at closer" (snow) or "Let's listen to the rain" (rain) If safe: go outside briefly to experience weather directly Or: "Let's create our own rain/snow inside!" Transition to weather-related activity Offer choice: "Weather art or weather experiment?" Stay engaged 10+ minutes DIY Alternative Tool: Rain/Snow Sensory Bottle Materials: Clear plastic bottle, water, glitter or small white beads (snow), oil, blue food coloring (rain) Cost: Under $5 How to Make:
For rain: water + blue coloring + glitter + oil For snow: water + white beads/glitter + clear oil Seal tightly Child tips bottle, watches "rain" or "snow" fall slowly inside Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Portable weather observation, child controls, reusable Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Active Weather Play Cost: $0-10 (weather gear) Materials: Raincoat, boots, umbrella (rain) or snow gear (snow) How to Use: Go outside during weather Jump in puddles Catch raindrops/snowflakes Make snow angels Active participation in weather Duration: 20-30 minutes Why it works: Active, outdoor, full sensory experience, not passive watching Rain/Snow Collection Project Cost: $0-5 (containers) Materials: Containers, measuring tools How to Use: Collect rainwater or snow Measure amount Watch snow melt, measure water Keep weather journal
Scientific observation Duration: 10 minutes collection + ongoing observations Why it works: Purpose-driven, educational, scientific Weather Art Projects Cost: $5-10 (art supplies) Materials: Paper, paints, spray bottles For Rain Art: Paint on paper Take outside in rain (brief) Rain creates patterns For Snow Painting: Spray bottles with colored water "Paint" in snow outside Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Creative, outdoor, produces art Weather Tracking Chart Cost: $2-5 (chart paper) Materials: Chart, markers, stickers How to Use: Create weather chart Mark daily weather (rain, snow, sun, clouds) Count rainy/snowy days per month Graph findings Makes weather observation purposeful Duration: 5 minutes daily + monthly graphing Why it works: Educational, long-term project, purposeful Precipitation Experiments Cost: $5-10 (materials) Materials: Various surfaces, measuring tools
How to Use: Test water absorption: which surface absorbs rain/snow fastest? Measure snowflake size Time how long snow takes to melt Scientific approach Duration: 30-60 minutes Why it works: Educational, hands-on science Alternative Stimulation (For AVOIDERS): Weather Pictures/Videos Cost: $0-10 (books or videos) Materials: Books about weather or calm weather videos How to Use: Look at pictures (no actual weather) Calm weather videos (can pause) Educational and controlled Duration: 10 minutes Why it works: No actual weather exposure, controllable Weather Sensory Bottle Cost: $3-5 Materials: Sensory bottle (described above) How to Use: Child controls "weather" in bottle Tip to make rain/snow fall Completely contained Predictable Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Child controls, contained, predictable Indoor Weather Sounds Cost: $0 (online sounds)
Materials: Rain/snow sounds recording How to Use: Listen to weather sounds indoors No visual component Calm, controlled Can adjust volume Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Auditory only (less overwhelming), controllable Distance Window Watching Cost: $0 Materials: Window view How to Use: Watch weather from inside Across room from window (distance) Very brief (1-2 minutes) Parent provides support Duration: 1-2 minutes Why it works: Distance reduces intensity, brief, supported Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Active Weather Engagement: Go outside during weather: Run in rain Jump in puddles Roll in snow Provides full body sensory input 20-30 minutes Weather-Based Movement: Pretend to be weather: "Rain" movements (arms down wiggling) "Snow" movements (spinning and falling) Vestibular + proprioceptive input 15-20 minutes Scheduled Weather Watching:
Brief observation times: Morning: 3 minutes weather watching Then: weather-related activity 15 minutes Prevents prolonged fixation For AVOIDERS: Indoor Weather Experience: Create weather inside (less overwhelming): Spray bottle "rain" in tub Shaved ice "snow" in bin Controlled, safe Gradual tolerance building Predictable Weather Routine: Same time, brief duration: "After breakfast: 2 minutes looking at rain" Very predictable Reduces anxiety about weather Preparation for Outdoor: Before going out in weather: Discuss what to expect Appropriate clothing Plan for quick return if needed Reduces anxiety Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Full Body Sensory Integration: After weather exposure: Full body massage Helps integrate weather sensory experience Calms if over-stimulated by weather Duration: 10 minutes Why it works: Weather provides intense multi-sensory input (tactile, visual, auditory, vestibular), massage helps integrate
Warming Massage: After cold weather exposure: Vigorous rubbing on arms/legs (creates warmth) Brings blood flow back Organizing and warming 5-7 minutes For AVOIDERS: Preparation Massage: Before weather exposure: Grounding, calming massage Firm pressure "You're safe, we'll stay together" Duration: 7-10 minutes Why it works: Prepares nervous system for potentially overwhelming weather experience Recovery After: After any weather exposure: Slow, deep pressure massage Weighted blanket Warm environment Helps recover from overwhelming experience 10-15 minutes Manifestation 7: Observing People Walking by Window Physical Redirection Technique: "People Watch Transition" Method Allow brief people watching (1-2 minutes) Acknowledge: "You see people walking!" After observation: "Let's count 3 more people, then we play" Count together: "1...2...3...okay, done watching" Before continued watching: physical redirect away from window
Offer related activity: "Let's play with people figurines" or "Let's look at family photos" Stay engaged with alternative If persistent: cover window temporarily or move to room without people view DIY Alternative Tool: People Action Cards Materials: Photos/drawings of people doing various activities, laminated cards Cost: $3-5 How to Make: Print or draw pictures of people walking, running, jumping, sitting Laminate if possible Child can look at cards instead of window Can sort by action, create stories Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Portable people observation without actual people, controllable Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): People Hunt Game Cost: $0-3 (paper, markers) Materials: Chart with different people types to spot How to Use: Create checklist: person with hat, person with dog, person running, etc.
Check off when spotted Time-limited (10 minutes) Makes watching purposeful Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Structured, game element, time-limited Play with People Figurines Cost: $10-20 (people figurines set) Materials: People figures, blocks/buildings How to Use: Create town/city Move people figures around Create scenarios Child controls all people movement Pretend play Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Child in control, pretend play, functional People Photography Project Cost: $0 (if have camera) Materials: Camera/phone How to Use: Take photos of people (with permission) Create photo book or collage Discuss different activities people do Art/learning project Duration: 15 minutes photography + project time Why it works: Active participation, creates product, purposeful "Where Are They Going?" Game Cost: $0 Materials: Window view How to Use:
Watch person walk by Guess where they're going Create story Adds imagination + cognitive element Time-limited Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Cognitive engagement, purposeful, structured People Movement Acting Cost: $0 Materials: Space to move How to Use: Watch person walk Child imitates their walk "Walk like that person" Different gaits, speeds Active participation Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Active, motor planning, not passive watching Alternative Stimulation (For AVOIDERS): People Picture Books Cost: $5-10 Materials: Books showing people in various activities How to Use: Look at pictures (not moving people) Read stories about people Calm, controlled Duration: 10 minutes Why it works: No actual people movement, predictable Family Photo Album Cost: $0-5 Materials: Photos of family members How to Use:
Look at familiar people In photos (not moving) Talk about family Comfort and familiarity Duration: 10 minutes Why it works: Familiar faces, no movement, calming Window Covering Cost: $0 Materials: Curtain, shade, or paper How to Use: Cover window when people traffic is high Reduces exposure if overwhelming Environmental modification Duration: As needed Why it works: Removes overwhelming stimulus Predictable People Time Cost: $0 Materials: Window, timer How to Use: "After breakfast: 2 minutes people watching" Timer marks end Same time daily Very brief Duration: 2 minutes Why it works: Time-limited, predictable Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Active People Play: After people watching: Play with action figures Create people scenarios Active pretend play 20-30 minutes Movement Activities: Imitate people movements:
Walk like different people Fast walk, slow walk, hop, run Gross motor + observation combined 15-20 minutes Social Skills Practice: Use people watching to teach: "That person is waving - let's practice waving" Social skills in safe context 10-15 minutes For AVOIDERS: Distance Observation: Watch from across room: Far from window Less intense Gradual approach over time Very gradual Predictable People Schedule: Know when people traffic is low: Mid-morning, mid-afternoon Plan activities away from window during busy times Environmental management Preparation: Before activities near window: "There might be people walking by" Discuss what to expect Plan coping strategies Reduces anxiety Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Visual Tracking Relief: After people watching: Gentle eye area massage (around eyes, not on) Temple massage Forehead smoothing
Relieves eye strain from tracking Duration: 5 minutes Why it works: Provides relief to eyes/visual system used in tracking people movement Neck Tension Release: Looking out window creates neck position: Massage neck (sides) Gentle rotations Shoulder massage 5-7 minutes For AVOIDERS: Grounding Before Window Time: If people watching is anxiety-inducing: Firm grounding pressure Shoulders, feet "You're safe, I'm here" Duration: 5 minutes Why it works: Prepares for potentially overwhelming social stimuli Calming After: After people exposure: Full body calming massage Deep pressure Quiet, private space Helps recover 10 minutes Manifestation 8: Tracking Pets Moving Around Room Physical Redirection Technique: "Pet Observation Transition" Method Allow brief pet tracking (2-3 minutes) Join child: "The cat is walking around!" After observation: "Let's count how many times kitty walks past, then we play"
Count 5 passes together Then: "Pet watching is done. Now let's play with toy animals" Offer related activity with toy animals or pet care task If persistent tracking: separate child and pet temporarily (pet in different room) Stay engaged with alternative 10+ minutes DIY Alternative Tool: Pet Movement Game Materials: Toy animals, paper, markers Cost: Under $5 How to Make/Use: Draw simple path/maze on large paper Child moves toy animal through path Can create different paths for different animals Child controls all movement Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Child controls animal movement, similar to watching pet but child-directed Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Active Pet Play Cost: $0-10 (pet toys) Materials: Pet-safe toys, treats How to Use: Play actively with pet
Throw ball for dog Use wand toy with cat Child engages pet in movement Child creates movement instead of just watching Duration: 20-30 minutes Why it works: Active participation, child initiates movement, bonding Pet Care Routine Cost: $0 (existing pet supplies) Materials: Food, water, grooming supplies How to Use: Child helps with pet care Fill water bowl, food bowl Brush pet (if appropriate) Take dog for walk Purposeful interaction Duration: 15-20 minutes daily Why it works: Functional, teaches responsibility, purposeful Pet Obstacle Course Cost: $0-10 (household items) Materials: Boxes, tunnels, toys How to Use: Create obstacle course for pet Guide pet through course Time trials Child actively engaging pet Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Active, child directs pet movement, problem-solving
Pet Behavior Journal Cost: $3-5 (notebook) Materials: Notebook, pencil, camera (optional) How to Use: Observe pet for 10 minutes daily Write/draw what pet does Take photos Scientific observation journal Makes watching purposeful Duration: 10-15 minutes observation + journal time Why it works: Educational, purposeful observation, creates product Toy Animal Play Cost: $10-20 (realistic animal toys) Materials: Animal figurines, habitat setup How to Use: Create animal habitat Move animals, create scenarios Pretend play Child controls all movement Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Similar to pet watching but child-controlled, pretend play Alternative Stimulation (For AVOIDERS): Pet Pictures/Videos Cost: $0-10 Materials: Photos of pets or calm pet videos How to Use: Look at still pet photos Or very calm, slow pet videos No actual moving pet
Controlled and predictable Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: No actual pet movement, controllable Stuffed Animal Instead Cost: $5-15 Materials: Stuffed animal that looks like pet How to Use: Child can hold, look at, carry No movement Predictable, comforting Addresses interest without live animal Duration: As needed Why it works: No movement, completely controllable, comfort object Predictable Pet Time Cost: $0 Materials: Pet, timer, structure How to Use: Scheduled "pet observation time" 3 minutes after lunch daily Timer shows when time ends Very predictable Duration: 3 minutes Why it works: Time-limited, predictable, structured Separate Spaces Cost: $0-30 (pet gate if needed) Materials: Baby gate or closed door How to Use: If pet movement is overwhelming Separate child and pet Environmental modification
Gradual reintroduction Duration: As needed Why it works: Reduces overwhelming stimulus Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Active Pet Engagement: Child engages pet actively: Throw toys Run with dog Pull string toy with cat Provides movement for child too 20-30 minutes Pet Care Integration: Make pet tracking purposeful: "Watch where dog goes to see if water bowl is empty" "See where cat sits to know if she's tired" Functional observation Throughout day Movement Imitation: Pretend to be pet: Walk on hands and feet like dog Stretch like cat Gross motor play 15-20 minutes For AVOIDERS: Gradual Pet Introduction: Week 1: Look at pet photos Week 2: Pet in same room but across the room Week 3: Pet closer but still separated by gate
Week 4: Brief interaction with support Very gradual Predictable Pet Routine: Pet has predictable schedule: Morning: pet in living room Afternoon: pet in bedroom Child knows where pet will be Reduces anxiety Child Controls Interaction: Child decides: Whether to be near pet How close to get When to leave Complete control Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Visual Tracking Relief: After pet watching: Eye area massage (around eyes) Temple massage Relieves visual tracking strain Duration: 5 minutes Why it works: Tracking moving pet uses visual system intensively, massage provides relief Full Body Calming: After active pet play: Full body massage Calms excitement Organizes after vigorous play 10 minutes For AVOIDERS: Preparation for Pet Interaction: Before time with pet: Grounding massage Firm pressure "Pet is safe, you're safe"
Duration: 5-7 minutes Why it works: Prepares nervous system for unpredictable pet movement Recovery After: After pet exposure: Calming full body massage Deep pressure Quiet environment Helps recover from unpredictable movement 10-15 minutes
Comprehensive Stimming Guide > 1. VISUAL STIMMING INTERVENTIONS > C. Self-Generated Visual Stimming > Level 1: Finger/Hand Visual Play
Causation: Over-stimulated: Self-generated predictable input blocks overwhelming environment Under-stimulated: Creates needed visual stimulation on demand Sensitivity: Complete control over visual input intensity and pattern Sensory Profile: Seeker: Fast, intense movements; long duration (10-30+ minutes) Avoider: Slower, controlled movements; shorter bursts (1-5 minutes) Description: Watching own hands/fingers create visual patterns Manifestation 1: Fluttering Fingers in Front of Eyes (Rapid, Sustained) Physical Redirection Technique: "Gentle Hand Lowering" Method Approach from side (don't block child's view suddenly) Gently place your hand over child's fluttering hand Slowly lower both hands together while saying "Hands down" Immediately place interesting textured object in child's hands (squishy ball, textured toy) Say: "Feel this instead" Guide hands to explore object If hands return to fluttering: repeat gently Stay engaged with tactile activity 5+ minutes
DIY Alternative Tool: Finger Dance Board Materials: Small mirror (6x6"), textured surfaces around mirror, LED tea light for backlighting Cost: Under $5 How to Make: Mount small mirror on cardboard backing Attach different textures around edges (fabric, sandpaper, bubble wrap, velvet) Optional: place LED light behind for visual interest Child can watch fingers move in mirror while also feeling textures Combines visual with tactile Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Provides visual input (mirror reflection) plus tactile input (textures), controlled environment Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Finger Light Show Cost: $5-10 (finger lights) Materials: LED finger lights (various colors) How to Use: Place finger lights on fingers Dark room Move fingers, watch light trails Create patterns in air "Dance" fingers to music
Intense visual + child controls Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Provides intense visual feedback for finger movements, adds purpose, time-limited Finger Paint Play Cost: $5-10 (finger paints) Materials: Finger paints, large paper How to Use: Child paints with fingers Watches fingers move AND feels texture Creates art Combines visual, tactile, creative Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Finger movement + tactile + visual + creative output Puppet Finger Theater Cost: $5-10 (finger puppets) Materials: Finger puppets, small stage area How to Use: Put puppets on fingers Create show Watch puppets (fingers) move Tell stories Functional finger movement Duration: 20-30 minutes Why it works: Purposeful finger movement, creative, social option Play-Doh Manipulation Cost: $3-5 (play-doh) Materials: Play-doh, tools How to Use:
Squeeze, roll, pinch play-doh Watch fingers working Create shapes Heavy tactile input to fingers Duration: 30-45 minutes Why it works: Intense tactile input may reduce finger fluttering need, purposeful Finger Games/Songs Cost: $0 Materials: Just hands and songs How to Use: "Itsy Bitsy Spider," "Where is Thumbkin?" Finger movement songs with purpose Can watch fingers while singing Structured finger movement Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Functional, structured finger movement, social/language component Alternative Stimulation (For AVOIDERS): Gentle Hand Massage Cost: $0 Materials: Lotion (optional) How to Use: Gentle hand massage instead of fluttering Slow, calming Addresses need for hand input Very soothing Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Provides tactile input without self-stimulation, calming Holding Comfort Object Cost: $5-10 (soft toy or blanket)
Materials: Soft comfort item How to Use: Give child something soft to hold Occupies hands Calming and soothing Prevents fluttering Duration: As needed Why it works: Hands occupied, calming, alternative sensory input Simple Hand Activity Cost: $3-5 (stress ball or fidget) Materials: One simple fidget toy How to Use: Squeeze stress ball Quiet, simple hand activity Not overwhelming Predictable Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Simple alternative, not overstimulating Hand Holding Cost: $0 Materials: Just hands How to Use: Hold child's hands gently Calming presence Prevents fluttering Soothing connection Duration: 3-5 minutes as needed Why it works: Physical comfort, hands occupied, calming Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Heavy Hand Work: Before finger fluttering typically occurs: Push hands into therapy putty
Squeeze stress balls Hand grip exercises 5-10 minutes provides organizing input May reduce fluttering by satisfying sensory need Bilateral Hand Activities: Activities using both hands together: Clapping games Throwing/catching Building with blocks Organizes both hands/brain hemispheres 15-20 minutes Scheduled "Hand Time": Designate times for hand-focused activities: Morning: 10 minutes finger painting Afternoon: 10 minutes play-doh Evening: 5 minutes finger games Provides hand/finger input at specific times For AVOIDERS: Gentle Hand Introduction: Very gradual hand activities: Week 1: Gentle hand massage only Week 2: Hold soft object Week 3: Simple hand activity (stress ball) Week 4: Brief finger game Extremely gradual Predictable Hand Routine: Same hand activity daily: "After breakfast: 5 minutes with soft ball" Very predictable Not demanding Reduces anxiety Hands Occupied Strategy:
Always provide something to hold: Comfort object Fidget toy Parent's hand Prevents fluttering through occupation Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Deep Finger and Hand Massage: Firm pressure on each finger (base to tip) Press on each finger joint (knuckles) Massage palm with firm circular pressure Squeeze hand firmly (like handshake but sustained) Pull gently on each finger (traction - provides joint input) Duration: 5-10 minutes per hand Frequency: 2-3x daily, especially BEFORE times when finger fluttering typically occurs (morning, after school, before bed) Why it works: Provides intense proprioceptive input to hands/fingers that are seeking stimulation, may significantly reduce finger fluttering behavior by satisfying underlying sensory need Bilateral Hand Compression: Press both hands together (prayer position) Child pushes hard Hold for count of 10
Repeat 5 times Organizing bilateral input 3-5 minutes For AVOIDERS: Gentle Hand Preparation: Very gentle hand massage Warm hands by rubbing together first Gentle circular motions on palms No deep pressure initially Duration: 3-5 minutes Frequency: Before any hand activities Why it works: Gentle preparation helps nervous system tolerate hand activities, reduces anxiety about touch Hand Wrapping: Wrap child's hand in soft cloth Gentle pressure through cloth Hold for count of 10 Very calming 3 minutes per hand Manifestation 2: Waving Hands While Watching Closely Physical Redirection Technique: "Wave and Engage" Method Join child briefly - wave your hands too (validates behavior) After 30 seconds: "Let's wave goodbye to hand waving!" Wave together as goodbye Immediately: "Now hands are going to..." (specific alternative)
Place textured object in hands OR guide to activity needing hand use "Let's clap instead!" or "Let's build with these blocks" If hands return to waving: gently redirect "Hands are building now" Stay engaged 5+ minutes DIY Alternative Tool: Wave-Activated Light Box Materials: Cardboard box, LED motion sensor light, hole for hands Cost: $8-12 How to Make: Cut hole in box for hand entry Place motion sensor LED light inside When child waves hands in box, light activates Creates immediate feedback for hand movement Purpose-driven waving Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Hand waving has immediate visual result, contained, purposeful Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Waving Flags/Scarves Cost: $5-10 (scarves or make flags) Materials: Colorful scarves or ribbon flags on sticks How to Use:

Comprehensive Stimming Guide > 1. VISUAL STIMMING INTERVENTIONS > C. Self-Generated Visual Stimming > Level 2: Eye-Based Stimming
Causation: Over-stimulated: Modifying visual input reduces overwhelm Under-stimulated: Creates visual patterns and stimulation Sensitivity: Exploring visual system capabilities; tic-like compulsion Sensory Profile: Seeker: Frequent, intense eye movements throughout day Avoider: Using to filter/block visual input Sensitivity: May have underlying visual processing issues Description: Using eye movements or focus to create visual effects Manifestation 1: Repetitive Blinking (Rapid, 2-3 Blinks Per Second) Physical Redirection Technique: "Blink Awareness" Method Don't draw attention to blinking initially (may increase it) If persistent: gently say "Let's rest our eyes" Guide child to calm activity with eyes closed briefly "Close eyes and count to 10" Then open eyes and engage in visual activity requiring focus (puzzle, book) If blinking continues: "Let's do something fun for eyes" (looking activity)
Engage in purposeful visual activity DIY Alternative Tool: Eye Rest Station Materials: Comfortable spot, soft eye mask, calming music Cost: $5-10 How to Make/Use: Create cozy spot for eye rest Soft eye mask available Calming music or sounds Child rests eyes when needed 3-5 minutes rest periods Duration: 3-5 minutes as needed Why it works: Gives eyes break, reduces eye strain that may cause blinking Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Eye Exercise Games Cost: $0 Materials: Just eyes How to Use: Look up, down, left, right (without blinking) Follow finger with eyes Eye "workout" that's purposeful Makes eye movement functional Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Purposeful eye movement, provides eye input in controlled way Looking Activities Cost: $0-5 Materials: "I Spy" books, Where's Waldo, hidden picture books
How to Use: Visual search activities Requires careful looking (less blinking) Engaging for eyes Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Eyes focused on task, purposeful Magnifying Glass Exploration Cost: $5-10 (magnifying glass) Materials: Magnifying glass, small objects to examine How to Use: Look closely at objects Requires sustained focus Engaging visual activity Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Sustained focus reduces rapid blinking Eye Yoga/Relaxation Cost: $0 Materials: Quiet space How to Use: Close eyes gently Imagine calming scene Eye relaxation exercises Reduces eye tension Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Directly addresses eye fatigue Alternative Stimulation (For AVOIDERS): Gentle Eye Rest Cost: $0 Materials: Quiet space How to Use: Close eyes gently for brief periods No pressure Just rest Duration: 3-5 minutes
Why it works: Simple, restful Soft Eye Mask Cost: $5-8 Materials: Soft, comfortable eye mask How to Use: Wear during rest time Complete darkness Very calming for eyes Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Blocks all visual input, very calming Dim Lighting Cost: $0 Materials: Dimmer switch or lamp control How to Use: Reduce lighting in environment Less strain on eyes May reduce blinking Duration: Throughout day as needed Why it works: Environmental modification, less eye strain Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Vision Therapy Activities: Activities to strengthen/organize vision: Eye tracking exercises Convergence exercises Focus near/far switching Consult with occupational therapist or vision therapist May reduce blinking by improving eye muscle control Regular Eye Breaks: 20-20-20 rule: Every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds
Reduces eye strain May reduce blinking Reduce Screen Time: Screens can increase blinking Limit screen time Take frequent breaks May significantly reduce blinking For AVOIDERS: Gentle Visual Environment: Reduce visual clutter Soft lighting Calm colors May reduce eye overwhelm causing blinking Regular Eye Rest: Scheduled quiet times with eyes closed "After lunch: 5 minutes quiet rest" Gives eyes regular breaks Medical Check: Rule out vision problems May need glasses Allergies can cause blinking Consult doctor if persistent Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Eye Area Massage (Very Gentle): NEVER touch eyeballs directly Very gentle massage around eyes Gentle circular motions on temples Gentle pressure above and below eyes (on bony area, not on eyes) Smooth across forehead Duration: 3-5 minutes Frequency: When blinking is excessive
Why it works: Releases tension around eyes, may reduce blinking tic IMPORTANT: Only do if child comfortable, never force, very gentle touch only Forehead and Temple Focus: Gentle circles on temples Smooth forehead outward from center Very calming for visual system 3-5 minutes For AVOIDERS: Gentle Face Touch: Very gentle touch on face (not near eyes unless child comfortable) Cheeks, forehead No pressure near eyes Very gentle and respectful 2-3 minutes Only if child tolerates Calming Touch: Gentle hands on shoulders (not face) Grounding touch away from face May be less threatening 3-5 minutes Manifestation 2: Crossing Eyes and Uncrossing Repeatedly Physical Redirection Technique: "Eye Position Redirect" Method Don't draw excessive attention to behavior Engage with activity requiring eyes to look straight ahead
"Look at this!" (hold object at child's midline, arm's length away) Activities requiring normal eye position: puzzles, reading, building If crossing continues: "Let's give eyes a rest" (close eyes briefly) Then re-engage with visual activity DIY Alternative Tool: Eye Tracking Board Materials: Board with moving element (marble in maze, sliding bead toy) Cost: $5-10 How to Make/Use: Board with visual tracking activity Child must keep eyes straight to track Engaging enough to maintain normal eye position Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Requires normal eye position for success Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Near-Far Focus Game Cost: $0 Materials: Two objects at different distances How to Use: Hold object close (1 foot) "Look at this" Then point to object far away (10+ feet)
"Now look at that" Switch back and forth Exercises eyes purposefully Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Purposeful eye exercise, builds eye muscle control Throwing and Catching Cost: $5 (ball) Materials: Ball appropriate for child's age How to Use: Throw and catch Eyes must track ball (normal position) Active and engaging Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Requires normal eye position, active Reading/Looking at Books Cost: $0-10 (books) Materials: Engaging books at appropriate level How to Use: Reading or looking at pictures Requires eyes in normal position Engaging activity Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Purposeful activity requiring normal eye position Vision Therapy Games Cost: $0-20 (simple supplies) Materials: Pencil, string, beads How to Use: String with bead: focus on bead while moving closer/farther
Pencil push-ups: focus on pencil tip while moving toward nose Vision therapy exercises Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Strengthens eye muscles, improves control Note: Best done under guidance of vision therapist or OT Alternative Stimulation (For AVOIDERS): Gentle Eye Activities Cost: $0 Materials: Quiet environment How to Use: Simple looking activities No pressure Brief durations Duration: 5 minutes Why it works: Low pressure, gentle Eye Rest Cost: $0 Materials: Quiet space How to Use: Close eyes for rest No visual demands Very calming Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Removes visual demands completely Sunglasses Cost: $5-15 Materials: Comfortable sunglasses How to Use: Wear indoors if needed Reduces visual input May reduce eye crossing Duration: As needed Why it works: Environmental modification
Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Vision Therapy: Consult with developmental optometrist or vision therapist Eye muscle exercises Convergence/divergence training May significantly reduce eye crossing Professional guidance important Engaging Visual Activities: Activities requiring sustained focus: Puzzles Building Reading Keeps eyes in functional position Regular Breaks: 20-20-20 rule (every 20 min, look 20 feet away, 20 seconds) Reduces eye fatigue For AVOIDERS: Reduce Visual Demands: Simplify visual environment Adequate rest Regular breaks from visual tasks May reduce eye crossing Medical Evaluation: Vision problems may cause crossing May need glasses Consult eye doctor Important to rule out medical causes Gentle Approach: Never force eye position Gentle encouragement only Medical/therapeutic support if needed Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Temple and Eye Area Massage: Very gentle massage on temples (circular motion)
Gentle pressure around eye orbital bones (NOT on eyes) Gentle pressure between eyebrows May help relax eye muscles Duration: 3-5 minutes Frequency: When eye crossing is frequent Why it works: Releases tension in eye muscles CAUTION: Very gentle only, never touch eyeballs, stop if uncomfortable Forehead Release: Smooth forehead outward from center Releases tension in forehead/eye area 3-5 minutes For AVOIDERS: Gentle Touch Near Face: Only if child tolerates Very gentle No pressure May skip face entirely 2-3 minutes if tolerated Alternative Grounding: Massage shoulders/feet instead of face Provides calming without face touch 5-7 minutes Manifestation 3: Looking at Things from Peripheral Vision Only Physical Redirection Technique: "Center Focus Redirect" Method Position yourself directly in child's center vision (unavoidable) Hold interesting object in center visual field
Say name to get attention "Look right here at this" (point to center object) When child looks centrally (even briefly), praise immediately: "Good looking!" Keep object central and engaging Activities requiring central vision: puzzles, books, building Stay engaged 10+ minutes DIY Alternative Tool: Central Vision Game Board Materials: Board with activities requiring direct looking (mirror, buttons, spinners in center) Cost: $5-10 How to Make: Mount activities in center of board Small mirror (must look directly) Buttons to push Spinner to watch All require looking straight at center Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Encourages central vision use through engaging activities Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Flashlight Target Game Cost: $2-5 (flashlight, targets) Materials: Flashlight, colored targets on wall How to Use: Call out color: "Hit the red target!"
Child must look directly at target to shine light accurately Score points for accuracy Requires central vision Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Game requires direct looking, engaging Eye Contact Games Cost: $0 Materials: Just people How to Use: Staring contests (who can look longest) "Look at my eyes" games Social eye contact practice Make it fun, not demanding Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Practices central vision socially Target Practice Cost: $5-10 (dart board with velcro darts or bean bag toss) Materials: Safe target, throwing objects How to Use: Must look directly at target to hit it Score points Competitive element Requires central vision for success Duration: 20-30 minutes Why it works: Functional central vision use Reading Activities Cost: $0-10 (books)
Materials: Books at appropriate level How to Use: Reading requires central vision Can't read from peripheral Engaging content Educational Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Necessary for reading, purposeful Mirror Activities Cost: $5-10 (mirror) Materials: Mirror How to Use: Look at self in mirror (requires central) Make faces Practice expressions Brush hair/teeth while watching Duration: 10-15 minutes Why it works: Must use central vision to see self Alternative Stimulation (For AVOIDERS): Brief Central Looking Cost: $0 Materials: Interesting object How to Use: Very brief central looking (1-2 seconds) No pressure Gradual increase Duration: 5 minutes practice Why it works: Very gradual, low pressure Favourite Object Central Cost: $0 Materials: Child's favourite toy How to Use: Hold favourite centrally Natural desire to look
Uses interest Duration: 3-5 minutes Why it works: Motivation through interest No Demands Cost: $0 Materials: Patient approach How to Use: Don't force central looking Accept peripheral looking Gradual encouragement only Duration: Ongoing Why it works: Reduces anxiety Supported Looking Cost: $0 Materials: Parent support How to Use: Parent gently turns child's face toward object (if tolerated) Very brief Very supported Duration: 1-2 minutes Why it works: Co-regulated Regulation Through Occupational Therapy: For SEEKERS: Vision Therapy: Professional vision therapy Central vision training exercises Tracking activities May significantly improve central vision use Consult developmental optometrist or OT with vision specialty Central Vision Games: All activities require central looking: Board games Card games Puzzles Reading Daily practice Social Skills Integration: Eye contact as social skill
Practice in safe context Builds central vision use For AVOIDERS: Very Gradual Approach: Week 1: Accept peripheral looking Week 2: Brief central glances (1 second) Week 3: Increase to 3 seconds Week 4: 5 seconds Months-long progression Medical Evaluation: Vision problems may cause peripheral preference May need glasses Rule out medical causes No Pressure: Never force Accept peripheral looking Gradual encouragement Professional support if needed Massage Techniques: For SEEKERS: Facial and Neck Massage: Gentle massage on face (if tolerated) Temples, cheeks, jaw Neck massage (sides) May help relax facial muscles affecting vision Duration: 5-7 minutes Frequency: Daily or when peripheral looking is dominant Why it works: Releases tension that may contribute to visual avoidance Eye Area Focus: Very gentle around eyes (NOT on eyes)
Orbital bone massage Above and below eyes 3-5 minutes For AVOIDERS: Avoid Face Touch: May be too overwhelming Focus on body massage instead Shoulders, arms, legs Provides organizing input without face touch 7-10 minutes Grounding Touch: Firm pressure on shoulders Grounding on feet Away from face 5-7 minutes Manifestation 4: Squinting to Blur Vision Intentionally Physical Redirection Technique: "Clear Vision Redirect" Method Gently say: "Let's open eyes wide and see clearly" Model opening eyes wide "Can you see this better with eyes open?" (show interesting object) Engage with clear-vision activities If squinting continues: "Eyes are working hard. Let's rest them" Brief eye rest, then re-engage Activities requiring clear vision: reading, puzzles, detailed looking DIY Alternative Tool: Clear/Blur Vision Comparison Materials: Pictures, some clear and some blurred versions Cost: $0-3 (print pictures) How to Make/Use:
Show clear vs blurred images Discuss difference "Which do you like better?" Help child become aware of vision choices Duration: 10 minutes Why it works: Builds awareness of vision control Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Blur-Clear Game Cost: $0 Materials: Just eyes How to Use: Intentional blur: squint Then clear: open wide Control practice "Blur...clear...blur...clear" Makes squinting purposeful and controlled Duration: 5-10 minutes Why it works: Gives control, makes it purposeful, time-limited Looking Through Different Materials Cost: $3-5 (cellophane, mesh, sheer fabric) Materials: Various see-through materials How to Use: Look through different materials See how vision changes Controlled blurring effect Can compare materials Duration: 15-20 minutes Why it works: Provides blur experience in controlled way Focus Near-Far Cost: $0 Materials: Objects at different distances

Comprehensive Stimming Guide > 1. VISUAL STIMMING INTERVENTIONS > C. Self-Generated Visual Stimming > Level 3: Body Position Visual Effects
Causation: Over-stimulated: Novel visual perspectives are organizing Under-stimulated: Creates intense, unusual visual input Sensitivity: Vestibular + visual integration need Sensory Profile: Seeker: Extreme positions, prolonged duration, intense spinning Mixed: Seeks vestibular + specific visual effects Description: Using whole body position to create visual experiences Manifestation 1: Lying on Back Watching Ceiling Fan Physical Redirection Technique: "Position Change" Method Approach lying child calmly "Time to sit up now" Gently help child to sitting position Immediately engage in sitting activity: puzzle, game, snack If resistance: "You can lie down later. Now we..." Keep engaged in different position 10+ minutes If lying down happens repeatedly: remove from room with ceiling fan DIY Alternative Tool: Desk Fan with Attachments Materials: Small desk fan, colorful ribbons, safe distance Cost: $10-15 How to Make/Use:
Desk fan at child's seated eye level Attach colorful ribbons to front (very securely) Child can watch while sitting More appropriate position Duration: 10-15 minutes (time-limited) Why it works: Provides fan watching in appropriate position Alternative Stimulation (For SEEKERS): Sitting Fan Activities Cost: $0-10 (existing fan or desk fan) Materials: Fan at appropriate level How to Use: Watch fan while sitting at table Time-limited (10 minutes) Then transition to other activity More appropriate than lying Duration: 10 minutes Why it works: Satisfies fan interest in better position Spinning Toys While Sitting Cost: $10-15 (various spinners) Materials: Tops, fidget spinners, gyroscopes How to Use: Sitting activities with spinning Similar visual but appropriate position Child controls spinning Duration: 20-30 minutes Why it works: Alternative to fan, good position
