Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Grocery helper: Child carries canned goods from car to house, makes multiple trips with heavy bags Laundry carrier: Assign child to carry full laundry baskets (wet clothes are heavier) from washer to dryer Book delivery: Carry stacks of books from one room to another, pile magazines to move, organize heavy items Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Bucket carries: Fill two buckets with water/sand (2-5 lbs each), carry across yard, empty, repeat 10-15 times Weighted vest wearing: Wear a weighted vest (5-10% body weight) during activities for 20-30 minutes Rock collection: Gather rocks outside, carry in containers, build rock piles, move them repeatedly For Avoiders: Light carrying: Start with very light objects, gradually increase weight over weeks Short distances: Carry heavy items only a few feet, not long distances
Choice-based: Child chooses what and when to carry, maintains control Massage Techniques: Shoulder and arm deep tissue: Massage shoulders, upper arms with deep pressure following direction of muscle fibers Upper back compression: Press firmly on upper back muscles for 10-second intervals Whole arm squeezes: Squeeze entire length of arm from shoulder to wrist rhythmically Manifestation 2: Pushing Furniture or Large Items Physical Redirect Technique: Stop the activity safely, kneel to eye level and say "You need strong pushing work. Let's find safe things to push." Set up approved pushing activities immediately - chair on carpet to specific spot, ottoman across room, etc. DIY Alternative Tool: Pushing Station: Fill a large cardboard box (3 ft x 2 ft) with heavy books or cans, wrap with duct tape for durability. Mark "START" and "FINISH" lines on floor (10-15 feet apart). Child pushes box back and forth 10 times. Can add/remove weight to adjust difficulty.
Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Dining chair pushes: Child pushes heavy dining chairs around table (on carpet for safety), sets table by pushing chairs to positions Couch rearranging: Assign child to help rearrange light furniture regularly (with supervision) Shopping cart pusher: At store, child pushes the shopping cart (with heavy items if possible) Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Wall pushes: Stand arm's length from wall, do 20-30 standing push-ups against wall Yoga ball pushes: Child and adult face each other, push large yoga ball back and forth with effort Animal walks: Bear walks (hands and feet, bottom up), crab walks, frog jumps across room 5-10 times For Avoiders: Light object pushing: Push empty boxes or very light furniture Assisted pushing: Adult helps push so child doesn't feel overwhelmed by weight
Short duration: Push for only 10-20 seconds, brief exposure Massage Techniques: Arm and shoulder compression massage: Compress shoulder muscles, then squeeze down entire arm length firmly Chest muscle release: Massage pectoral muscles (chest) with firm circular motions, 2-3 minutes Upper body sports massage: Use same techniques as athletic massage focusing on pushing muscles Manifestation 3: Climbing Repetitively (Stairs, Playground equipment, Furniture) Physical Redirect Technique: Approach the climbing child, ensure safety, and say "I see you're working hard climbing. Let's make a climbing challenge." Create structured climbing activity - up and down stairs 5 times, or climb playground equipment with specific route, rest, repeat. DIY Alternative Tool: Indoor Climbing Path: Use furniture and cushions to create approved climbing circuit. Mark path with colored tape arrows on floor. Child follows path: climb over couch arm, crawl under table, climb onto ottoman, down, repeat circuit 5 times. Change course weekly.
Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Stair climbing: Assign child to go up and down stairs for specific purposes 10-15 times daily - retrieve items from upstairs, deliver messages, fetch laundry Ladder activities: Under supervision, child climbs a stepladder up and down, hands items to adult on top, promotes safe climbing Furniture obstacle course: Create approved furniture climbing route where child may climb safely Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Playground time: Daily playground visits with focus on climbing structures, 30-45 minutes Rock climbing: Indoor rock climbing walls (many gyms offer child programs), once weekly if possible Tree climbing: Supervised tree climbing in safe tree with low branches, teach safety rules For Avoiders: Step climbing only: Use single step or low platform, step up and down
Ramp walking: Walk up ramps or gentle inclines instead of climbing Ground activities: All activities stay on ground level, no height involved Massage Techniques: Full leg massage: Massage legs from hip to ankle with firm pressure, following muscle groups Calf and thigh compressions: Squeeze leg muscles firmly, hold 5 seconds, release, repeat down entire leg Lower back massage: Massage lower back muscles (climbing uses these) with firm circular motions Manifestation 4: Hanging from Arms for Extended Periods Physical Redirect Technique: Stand near child for safety, place hand near their back and say "Let's time your hang today." Count or use a timer to 30 seconds, encourage them to release and rest for 60 seconds, then hang again. Create interval hanging pattern: 30 sec hang / 60 sec rest / repeat 5 times.
DIY Alternative Tool: Timed Hanging Chart: Install an over-door pull-up bar securely. Create a chart tracking hang times (start with 10 seconds, work up to 30 seconds). Use timer app on phone. Child records their times. Place thick gym mat or folded blankets underneath for safety. Set rule: maximum 30 seconds per hang, must rest between. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Towel pull-ups: Drape sturdy towel over pull-up bar, child grabs towel ends and hangs from towel (less stress on hands) Monkey bar practice: Take child to playground specifically for monkey bar activities, 15-20 minutes Doorframe hangs: If doorframe is stable and child is light enough, brief hangs from doorframe (5-10 seconds only) Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Swimming: Swimming provides total body input including arm work similar to hanging, 2-3x weekly ideal
Climbing class: Enroll in climbing or gymnastics class offering structured hanging activities Resistance band arm work: Pull resistance bands in various directions, 20-30 reps, works same muscles as hanging For Avoiders: No hanging: Redirect to activities without hanging component Arm exercises seated: Arm strengthening while sitting (bicep curls with light weights) Brief touches only: Just touch the bar briefly without hanging weight Massage Techniques: Shoulder and upper back deep massage: Focus on shoulder girdle muscles with very firm pressure, 5 minutes Arm decompression: Hold arm while gently pulling/stretching in socket to decompress joint Hand and forearm massage: Massage hands, wrists, forearms with firm pressure (these take strain from hanging) Manifestation 5: Spontaneous Exercise (Push-ups, Sit-ups, Planks) Physical Redirect Technique: Join the child in 3-5 repetitions of whatever they're doing, then say "Great workout! Let's do a proper exercise set together." Lead them through structured routine with rest periods: 10 push-ups, rest 30 seconds, 10 sit-ups, rest 30 seconds, 30-second plank, done.
DIY Alternative Tool: Exercise Dice: Create cube from cardboard, write different exercises on each side (push-ups, sit-ups, jumping jacks, plank, squats, arm circles). Child rolls dice, does that exercise 10 times, rolls again. Makes exercise intentional rather than random. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Furniture exercises: Use sturdy chair for tricep dips (10 reps), couch for decline push-ups (10 reps), wall for wall sits (30 sec) Stair exercises: Run up stairs 5 times, do 10 step-ups on bottom step, do calf raises on step Water bottle weights: Fill two water bottles equally (start with 8 oz), use as hand weights for arm exercises Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Structured workout time: Set two 15-minute "workout times" daily with specific routine, prevents random exercising throughout day
Intense physical activity: Enroll in sports (soccer, martial arts, swimming) providing vigorous physical outlet Mini trampoline: Small trampoline (3 ft diameter) for jumping, provides intense proprioceptive input, 10-15 minutes daily For Avoiders: Gentle movement: Slow yoga, stretching, walking - not intense exercise Short duration: 2-3 minutes of gentle activity maximum Low energy: Calm activities that don't elevate heart rate much Massage Techniques: Sports massage technique: Massage all major muscle groups (legs, arms, back, shoulders) using firm kneading motions Post-exercise stretching: Gently stretch each muscle group while massaging, 30 seconds per area Ice massage: After intense exercise, massage muscles with ice (wrapped in cloth) for 5 minutes to reduce inflammation Manifestation 6: Wrestling or Rough Play Seeking Physical Redirect Technique: If play is getting unsafe, call "freeze!" Have everyone hold position, take breath, then say "Let's wrestle with rules." Set up safe wrestling space (on mat/carpet), establish rules (no hitting, stop when someone says stop), set 2-minute rounds with 1-minute breaks.
DIY Alternative Tool: Wrestling Mat Area: Designate specific carpeted area or use yoga mats (2-3 connected). Create boundary with colored tape. Post simple rules sign: "1. Stop when asked, 2. No hitting, 3. Adult watches, 4. 2-minute rounds." Wrestling only allowed in this space with supervision. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Pillow wrestling: Use couch pillows only, wrestle gently, safe impact Sumo wrestling: Both people wear oversized clothing stuffed with pillows, wrestle carefully Furniture moving together: Parent and child work together moving heavy furniture, provides similar resistance Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Martial arts class: Enroll in judo, wrestling, Brazilian jiu-jitsu classes providing structured contact Crash pad: Create safe crash area (pile of cushions/pillows), child can jump and crash into repeatedly Resistance play: Play tug-of-war, push against each other's hands, wheelbarrow races
For Avoiders: No contact: Avoid all wrestling and rough play Gentle games: Play board games, calm activities, reading together Personal space: Teach and maintain clear personal space boundaries Massage Techniques: Full body deep tissue massage: Work through all major muscle groups with very firm pressure, 10-15 minutes Joint compressions: Compress each major joint (shoulders, elbows, knees, ankles) firmly, 10 seconds each Myofascial release: Use knuckles or massage tool to apply sustained pressure to tight areas for 30-60 seconds Manifestation 7: Digging, Shovelling, Raking Excessively Physical Redirect Technique: Approach child with a specific task: "Your body needs digging work. I have a special job for you." Assign bounded task - dig a specific hole in a specific place, rake one specific area, shovel sand from one container to another. Provide clear stopping point.
DIY Alternative Tool: Digging Station: Fill a large plastic storage bin (20-30 gallon) with play sand or dirt. Hide small toys inside. Provide small shovel, rake, and spoon. Child digs to find toys, 15-20 minutes daily. Place bin outside or on tarp indoors. This contains the digging to appropriate space. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Sandbox time: Create small sandbox in corner of yard, child can dig freely for 30 minutes daily Garden helper: Assign real garden tasks - dig holes for planting, rake leaves, shovel mulch Rice/bean dig box: Fill large bin with dried rice or beans, hide objects, child digs with hands or cups Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Beach trips: Regular beach visits for unlimited sand digging (natural sensory paradise)
Dirt play: Allow muddy play in designated area, digging in real dirt is very satisfying Construction play: Toy dump trucks, diggers in sand, lets them "work" for extended periods For Avoiders: Clean sensory bins: Use clean materials (rice, pasta) instead of dirt, less messy Scooping activities: Scoop with cups rather than digging with hands, less intense Short exposure: Only 3-5 minutes of digging activity, brief participation Massage Techniques: Arm and shoulder massage: Deep massage of arms, shoulders, upper back (digging muscles), 5-10 minutes Hand strengthening massage: Massage palms, fingers with firm pressure, focuses on grip strength areas Forearm release: Massage forearm muscles (used heavily in digging) with sustained pressure Manifestation 8: Moving Slowly Against Resistance (Water, Sand) Physical Redirect Technique: Join child in the activity briefly, then say "Let's make this resistance work a game." Create challenges - walk through water heel-to-toe to other side, make specific patterns in sand while walking, count steps through resistant medium.
DIY Alternative Tool: Resistance Walking Path: If you have a pool, create underwater obstacle course with pool noodles, balls to push underwater, items to retrieve from bottom. If no pool, fill a kiddie pool with water (6-8 inches deep), child walks/marches through it for 10 minutes daily. Or create "sand path" in yard where child must walk. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Weighted vest walking: Child wears weighted backpack (3-5 lbs) while walking around house/yard, creates resistance Resistance band walking: Tie resistance band around waist, hold other end or attach to starting point, child walks forward Pushing heavy objects: Push laundry basket filled with books across carpet, provides similar resistance Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Swimming: Perfect activity providing total body resistance, 2-3x weekly ideal
Walk through tall grass: Walking through unmowed grass or field provides resistance Snow activities: In winter, walking, playing in deep snow provides amazing proprioceptive input For Avoiders: Smooth walking: Walk on regular ground with no resistance Light materials: If must use resistance, very light materials only Brief exposure: 30 seconds to 1 minute maximum of resistance activity Massage Techniques: Leg massage focus: Deep massage of all leg muscles from hip to ankle, 5-10 minutes Aquatic massage concept: If possible, massage child's limbs while in bathtub, water provides different sensation Lower body compression: Compress leg muscles firmly, simulating the pressure of moving through water/sand
Comprehensive Stimming Guide > 4. PROPRIOCEPTIVE STIMMING > B. Postural Stimming > Level 1: Position Changes
Causation: Over-stimulated: Movement helps focus and attention Under-stimulated: Body needs constant position changes for input Sensitivity: Difficulty maintaining posture; muscles fatigue quickly Attention: Movement aids cognitive processing Sensory Profile: Seeker: Constant movement throughout all activities Fidgety: Can't maintain static position; not defiance Mixed: Vestibular + proprioceptive seeking Description: Frequently changing body positions Manifestation 1: Shifting Seating Position Constantly (every 30-120 seconds) Physical Redirect Technique: Place hand gently on child's shoulder, make eye contact and say "I notice your body needs to move. Let's do 5 chair push-ups together." Child places hands on chair sides, lifts bottom up 1-2 inches, lowers, repeat 5 times. This satisfies movement need briefly. DIY Alternative Tool: Seat Cushion Options: Make or use wobbly seating: DIY wobble cushion: Partially inflate beach ball (8-10 inches), place in pillowcase, tie closed. Child sits on this, allows movement while staying in seat.
Bumpy cushion: Place non-slip shelf liner or bubble wrap (bubble side up) on chair, provides texture to shift against. Resistance band chair: Tie exercise band around two front chair legs, child pushes feet against it while sitting. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Fidget tools at desk: Provide stress ball, putty, or fidget toy to squeeze with hands while sitting Foot fidget: Place small box under desk, child can rest/press/move feet against it Cushion variety: Let child choose from 2-3 different seat cushions each time they sit (gives sense of control) Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Movement breaks: Every 15-20 minutes, child stands, does 10 jumping jacks, sits back down Standing desk option: Use high table or counter for homework/activities, child stands and moves freely
Active sitting: Use therapy ball as chair (must be right size - feet flat on floor when sitting) For Avoiders: Stable seating: Provide very stable, comfortable chair with armrests Supported positions: Add pillows or cushions so child feels fully supported Predictable setup: Keep seating arrangement exactly the same, no changes Massage Techniques: Lower back massage: Child sits forward, massage lower back muscles with circular motions, 2-3 minutes (sitting uses these muscles) Hip flexor release: Massage front of hip area where leg meets torso, relieves sitting tension Glute massage: Massage gluteal muscles (seated position tires these), 2 minutes each side Manifestation 2: Standing Up and Sitting Down Repeatedly (10 –50+ times) Physical Redirect Technique: Approach calmly and say "I see you need up and down movement. Let's do it properly." Lead them through 10 controlled squats (stand, sit, stand, sit) counting together. Say "Now you can sit for 15 minutes" and set a timer. When timer goes off, repeat squats.
DIY Alternative Tool: Stand-Sit Chart: Create visual schedule showing sitting and standing periods. Use green and red cards. Green = stand time (2-3 minutes), red = sit time (15-20 minutes). Child flips cards themselves, giving control over transitions. Or use phone timer with different sounds for stand vs sit times. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Stand-up desk: Use counter or high table as standing work surface, child can shift weight while working Stool with no back: Use a backless stool, easier to stand up from, can rock on it Cushion removal: Remove chair cushion, makes standing up easier when urge hits Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Squats schedule: Set times (every 30 minutes) when child must do 10 squats, satisfies the need predictably
Chair aerobics: Child sits, stands, sits, stands 20 times as "exercise" before settling to sit Sit-stand desk: If possible, invest in adjustable height desk child can raise/lower For Avoiders: Stay seated: Provide activities that don't require transitions Minimize position changes: Organize space so child rarely needs to stand up Comfortable seating: Very comfortable chair makes staying seated more appealing Massage Techniques: Quad massage: Massage front thigh muscles (quadriceps) which work hard in standing/sitting, 2 minutes per leg Calf compressions: Squeeze calf muscles from knee to ankle, these stabilize standing Lower leg massage: Full lower leg massage focusing on muscles that lift body from sitting to standing Manifestation 3: Lying Down, Sitting Up, Lying Down Pattern Physical Redirect Technique: Approach during sitting phase, touch child's arm gently and say "Your body keeps moving. Let's do a body scan." Have them lie down intentionally, starting at head, tense and relax each body part (head, shoulders, arms, belly, legs, feet), takes 2-3 minutes. Often satisfies the position change need.
DIY Alternative Tool: Position Rotation Timer: Use phone timer or visual timer (Time Timer). Set for specific position durations: Lying: 5 minutes (green card) Sitting: 10 minutes (yellow card) Standing/moving: 3 minutes (red card) Child follows rotation, gets movement need met in structured way. Place yoga mat as designated "lying space." Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Floor desk: Set up floor workspace with clipboard or lap desk, child can work while lying down legitimately Reclining position: Use couch or recliner that allows semi-reclined position (compromise between lying and sitting) Multiple work stations: Set up 3 different work areas (desk, floor space, counter), child rotates between them Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Yoga sequence: Teach simple sequence moving through positions - child's pose (lying), table top (all fours), downward dog (inverted), repeat 5-10 times
Core strengthening: Lying activities that work core muscles (leg lifts, crunches), makes lying productive Floor time legitimized: Designate "floor work time" where lying down while working is acceptable For Avoiders: Stable positions only: Discourage position changes, keep one comfortable position Supported transitions: Use pillows and cushions during any position changes Slow transitions: Move very slowly between positions, no sudden changes Massage Techniques: Full body massage: Since child moves through many positions, massage entire body, 10 minutes, all muscle groups Transition massage: Massage the muscles used in position changes (core, hip flexors, back), 5 minutes Relaxation massage: Slow, rhythmic massage encouraging relaxation in one position Manifestation 4: Changing Legs Crossed Position Constantly Physical Redirect Technique: Kneel beside child, point to their legs and say "I see your legs need movement. Let's stretch them." Have child stand, do 10 leg swings (front to back, then side to side) each leg. Then return to sitting with both feet flat on floor for 15 minutes.
DIY Alternative Tool: Foot Fidget Box: Place a small cardboard box or bin under desk/table with different textures inside: Tennis ball (roll under feet) Bubble wrap (pop with toes) Resistance band (loop around chair legs, push with feet) Small textured mat (rub feet on) Child fidgets with feet instead of crossing/uncrossing legs. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Foot roller: Use rolling pin, water bottle, or tennis ball under feet while sitting - rolls back and forth Stool for feet: Provide small stool or box for feet rest, changes leg position without crossing Floor textures: Place different textured rug or mat under desk, feet get sensory input from rubbing on it Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Leg exercises at desk: Every 20 minutes, child does 10 seated leg lifts per leg (straighten leg, lift, lower)
Foot press: Loop resistance band around desk/chair legs, child pushes feet out against resistance while sitting Standing break: Every 30 minutes, stand and march in place 30 seconds For Avoiders: Comfortable footrest: Provide proper footrest at correct height, feet stay in one comfortable position Legs straight: Encourage keeping legs straight out, no crossing Minimal movement: Activities designed to keep legs still and comfortable Massage Techniques: Leg massage seated: While child sits, massage their legs from thigh to ankle, 2 minutes per leg Hip joint massage: Massage around hip joint area, 1-2 minutes per side (legs moving from hip) Foot massage: Massage bottoms of feet firmly, 2 minutes each (grounding and organizing) Manifestation 5: Moving from Chair to Floor to Furniture Physical Redirect Technique: As child moves to new surface, follow them and say "You're exploring different spots. Let's find your best working spot." Test 3 different positions (chair, floor with cushion, bean bag) by having child stay in each for 2 minutes with a simple task. Identify which feels best, encourage them to stay there for 20 minutes before changing.
DIY Alternative Tool: Three-Station Setup: Legitimize multiple work areas: Station 1: Regular desk/table with chair Station 2: Floor space with clipboard or lap desk, cushion to sit on Station 3: Low table with floor cushion or bean bag Set timer - 15 minutes per station. Child rotates through during longer activities. Makes movement part of the plan. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Large floor cushion: Provide big comfortable floor cushion, makes floor sitting more legitimate Lap desk: Wooden or hard lap desk allows work from anywhere (couch, floor, chair) Furniture arrangement: Arrange furniture so child can easily move between approved surfaces Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Obstacle course routine: Before settled work time, child completes obstacle course going on/over/under furniture, 5 minutes
Surface transitions: Make a game - sit on 5 different surfaces for 1 minute each, then pick favorite for work Body awareness: Each position change, name the position "I'm on the floor in criss-cross-applesauce," helps awareness For Avoiders: One stable location: Identify single most comfortable spot, use only that location Avoid transitions: Plan activities so child never needs to move to different surface Familiar setup: Keep exact same setup every time, no variation Massage Techniques: Universal massage: Full body massage since child uses all muscles moving through positions, 10 minutes Hip and lower back focus: These areas work hard during position changes, 3-5 minutes focused massage Stretching massage: Combine gentle stretching with massage at each joint Manifestation 6: Fidgeting in Seat (Squirming, Sliding, Repositioning)
Physical Redirect Technique: Place hand on desk near child (not touching them directly) and say "Pause - reset your body." Guide them to: plant both feet flat on floor, sit back fully in chair, place hands on desk, take 3 deep breaths. Say "Now you're reset" - often stops fidgeting briefly. DIY Alternative Tool: Sensory Seat Modifications: Bungee band: Tie thick resistance band or bungee cord around two front legs of chair (stretched), child pushes feet against band for fidgeting outlet Seat marker: Use velcro dots or non-slip mat to mark where bottom should sit, provides tactile cue Wobble disk: Use partially inflated cushion under bottom, allows movement while seated Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Hand fidgets: Provide quiet fidgets (stress ball, putty, smooth stone) for hands while sitting
Velcro under desk: Stick rough velcro strip under desk edge, child rubs fingers on it Gum chewing: If allowed, chewing gum provides oral motor input that reduces other fidgeting Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Pre-sitting heavy work: Before seated tasks, child does 10 push-ups, 10 squats, and runs in place 30 seconds Wiggle time: Every 15 minutes, child gets 1 minute to wiggle, squirm, move freely, then reset Therapy ball chair: Sit on therapy ball allowing bouncing and movement while maintaining seated position For Avoiders: Supportive seating: Chair with arms, high back, footrest - very stable and supportive Calm environment: Reduce environmental stimulation that might trigger fidgeting Short sitting periods: Only 10-minute seated periods, then break Massage Techniques: Quick seated massage: Massage shoulders and upper back while child stays seated, 2 minutes
Pressure on shoulders: Place hands on shoulders with firm downward pressure for 10 seconds, organizing Hand massage: Quick hand massage (1 minute each hand) at desk, grounding Manifestation 7: Kneeling, Then Sitting, Then Standing in Cycles Physical Redirect Technique: When you notice the cycling, approach and say "Your body needs lots of different positions. Let's try each one the best way." Guide them through proper form of each: kneel on cushion (1 min), sit correctly (2 min), stand and stretch (30 sec). Then encourage staying in sitting for longer period. DIY Alternative Tool: Position Cushion Set: Create stack of cushions for each position: Kneeling pad: Thick cushion or folded towel for comfortable kneeling Sitting cushion: Firm cushion for proper sitting Standing mat: Non-slip mat for standing position Child uses appropriate cushion for each position, makes transitions more intentional.
Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Adjustable workspace: Use surfaces at different heights (floor for kneeling, desk for sitting, counter for standing) Yoga mat: Provide yoga mat, child can kneel, sit, or lie on it comfortably Furniture variety: Use different furniture naturally supporting different positions (stool, chair, floor cushion) Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Position yoga: Teach sequence moving through positions - kneeling (child's pose), sitting (criss-cross), standing (mountain pose), repeat 10 times Assigned position changes: "Work 5 minutes kneeling, 10 minutes sitting, 2 minutes standing" - makes it structured Core strengthening: Positions changes require core strength, build core with planks, bridges For Avoiders: One position only: Pick most comfortable position, stay there entire time Supported positions: Add cushions, pillows supporting each position tried
Minimal transitions: Plan day to avoid need for position changes Massage Techniques: Knee and hip massage: These joints work hard during position changes, massage around them (not directly on joint), 2 minutes each Ankle massage: Massage ankles and feet which stabilize all three positions, 2 minutes each Quad and hamstring massage: Massage front and back of thighs which control position changes, 3 minutes Manifestation 8: Never Maintaining One Position More Than 2-3 Minutes Physical Redirect Technique: Use a visual timer (Time Timer or phone timer child can see). Say "Let's see if you can hold still while this timer runs." Start with 3 minutes. When successful, add 1 minute next time. Build gradually to 15-20 minutes. Provide immediate reward/break after timer completes.
DIY Alternative Tool: Incremental Position Timer: Use visual timer app or sand timer Start: 3 minutes in one position (achievable) Success: Move to 4 minutes Build by 1 minute as child succeeds Provide sticker or check mark for each success Display progress chart showing improvement **Alternative Stimulation (Household Items ):** Engaging activities: Use highly engaging activities (favorite video, compelling book) that naturally encourage staying still longer Reward system: Small immediate reward (sticker, high-five, 1 minute preferred activity) after holding position Position support: Make position as comfortable as possible (cushions, proper height, good lighting) Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Heavy input before stillness: 5 minutes of intense activity (running, jumping, pushing) right before need to be still Weighted lap pad: Place 3-5 lb lap pad on child during seated activities, helps maintain position
Isometric exercises: While in position, squeeze muscles (not visible) - squeeze fists, press feet into floor, provides input without moving For Avoiders: No pressure: Don't require long stillness periods Comfort priority: Make position so comfortable they naturally want to stay Short expectations: Only expect 5-10 minutes maximum in one position Massage Techniques: Pre-activity calming massage: Before need to sit still, 5-minute calming massage to organize nervous system Full body proprioceptive input: Firm massage of all body parts to increase body awareness, 10 minutes Rhythmic massage: Use slow, rhythmic strokes that have calming, organizing effect
Comprehensive Stimming Guide > 4. PROPRIOCEPTIVE STIMMING > B. Postural Stimming > Level 2: Unusual Positioning
Causation: Over-stimulated: Unusual positions provide unique organizing input Under-stimulated: Seeks novel proprioceptive sensations Sensitivity: Hypermobile joints allow greater range; seeking end-ranges Body Awareness: Exploring physical capabilities and limitations Sensory Profile: Seeker: Constantly trying new positions Flexible: May have joint hypermobility allowing extreme positions W-Sitting: Provides stability for poor core strength (requires correction) Description: Using atypical body positions Manifestation 1: Sitting with Legs in W position Physical Redirect Technique: Approach child from the side, gently touch their shoulder and say "Time to fix your legs." Physically help them move legs from W to criss-cross position or legs out front. Do this EVERY time you see W-sitting - consistency is crucial. Say "Legs need to be strong, W-sitting makes them weak." DIY Alternative Tool: Position Reminder System:
Visual cue: Place small stuffed animal or beanbag in front of child. If they can't see it over their knees, they're in W-position Sitting marks: Use colored tape on floor showing proper leg positions (criss-cross outline, side-sitting outline) Cube reminder: Make cube with pictures of correct sitting positions on each side, keep near child Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Sitting ring: Create ring from pool noodle (connect ends with tape), child sits in center, ring physically blocks W-position Cushion barrier: Place firm cushion between child's legs, prevents W-sitting Chair use: Encourage chair sitting instead of floor sitting to eliminate W-sitting entirely Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Core strengthening: W-sitting indicates weak core. Do planks, bridges, superman pose daily (10 reps each) Alternative floor positions: Practice 5 different sitting positions properly (criss-cross, legs out, side-sit, long-sit), master all of them
Balance activities: Stand on one foot (30 sec per foot), walk on balance beam, hop on one foot - builds leg strength For Avoiders: Chair sitting: Just use chairs, avoid floor sitting altogether Supported floor sitting: Sit against wall or furniture for back support, makes proper positioning easier Bean bag: Bean bag naturally prevents W-sitting while still providing floor-level experience Massage Techniques: Hip abductor massage: Massage outer thigh muscles firmly, 2 minutes each leg (these weaken in W-sitting) Hip rotator massage: Massage deep hip muscles (buttocks area), 2 minutes each side (these tighten in W-sitting) Leg length massage: Full leg massage from hip to ankle encouraging proper alignment, 3 minutes each Manifestation 2: Draping Body Over Furniture (Arms hanging, Body Draped)
Physical Redirect Technique: Approach child, gently touch their back and say "I see you need to hang. Let's do it safer." Guide them to lie across a large therapy ball (if available) or over several firm cushions stacked properly, achieving similar sensation safely. DIY Alternative Tool: Draping Station: Create safe draping opportunities: Therapy ball: Large yoga/therapy ball (appropriate size - child's feet touch ground when sitting), child lies over it on stomach Cushion stack: Stack 3-4 firm couch cushions, child drapes over safely Ottoman drape: Designate specific ottoman as "draping spot" with cushioning underneath Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Bean bag drape: Large bean bag chair, child can drape over side safely Bed edge: Child lies perpendicular on bed, upper body hangs over edge safely (adult supervision, not too long)
Couch arm rest: If sturdy, child drapes briefly over padded armrest Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Inverted positions: Safe inversions like downward dog yoga pose (makes triangle with body), hold 30 seconds Hanging activities: Safe hanging from approved bars (playground, pull-up bar) 10-30 seconds Forward folds: Standing, bend at waist, let arms and head hang down, 30 seconds For Avoiders: Upright positions only: Avoid any draping or inverted positions Seated forward bend: If must bend, only gentle forward bend while seated No head-down: Keep head level with or above heart at all times Massage Techniques: Back extension massage: Massage back muscles that work to maintain draping position, 3-5 minutes Abdominal massage: Massage stomach muscles (gently) which stretch during draping, 2 minutes
Spinal mobility massage: Massage alongside spine encouraging healthy spinal movement, 5 minutes Manifestation 3: Lying Upside Down on Furniture Physical Redirect Technique: Approach calmly, touch child's leg and say "I see you want upside-down feeling. Let's do it properly." Help them lie on couch/bed with head hanging back off edge (supported) for just 30-60 seconds. Set timer. Explain "Too long upside down isn't safe." DIY Alternative Tool: Controlled Inversion Station: Ramp cushion: Stack cushions in ramp shape, child lies on incline with head lower than feet (gentler inversion) Inversion timer: Use visible timer, child can be inverted only while timer runs (30-60 seconds), then must flip over Yoga mat spot: Designate yoga mat as "upside down spot," only allowed there with timer
Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Legs up wall: Child lies on floor, scoots bottom to wall, puts legs straight up wall (gentle inversion, very safe) Pillow prop: Lie on floor, place folded pillows under hips, elevating lower body above head slightly Recliner lean-back: Use recliner in full recline position, head lower than normal but not fully inverted Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Somersaults: Forward rolls on soft surface (5-10 repetitions) provides brief inversion Handstands against wall: With supervision, practice handstands or headstands against wall, 5-10 seconds Cartwheel practice: Learning cartwheels provides repeated brief inversions For Avoiders: No inversions: Avoid all head-down positions Slight recline only: Gentle recline (head still above heart) is maximum Upright preference: Stick to sitting and standing positions Massage Techniques:
Neck and shoulder massage: Inversions strain neck, massage these areas thoroughly, 3-5 minutes Scalp massage: Improve blood flow to head with firm scalp massage, 2 minutes Upper spine massage: Massage upper back and neck junction, 2-3 minutes Manifestation 4: Sitting in Tiny Spaces (Berween Cusions/Boxes) Physical Redirect Technique: Approach the small space, kneel at opening and say softly "Your body likes tight squeezes. I have a better squeeze place for you." Guide them to an approved tight space you've created (box fort, tent, compression spot between cushions). DIY Alternative Tool: Approved Small Spaces: Cardboard box fort: Large appliance box, cut door, add pillows inside, child's personal "squeeze space" Under-table tent: Drape blankets over table, add cushions inside, creates cave-like space Closet corner: Clear out corner of closet, add cushion and small light, approved squeeze spot
Pop-up tent: Small play tent (3-4 ft) child can fit inside comfortably Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Between couch cushions: Remove cushions, child sits in the space between, replace cushions lightly on sides Laundry basket: Large laundry basket with blanket over top, child sits inside with opening Sleeping bag: Zip child into sleeping bag, provides all-around compression Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Compression activities: Burrito roll in blanket (roll tightly), sandwich between cushions, 5-10 minutes Small space legitimized: Designate specific small spaces as acceptable, child can use when needed Body sock: Purchase lycra body sock, child climbs inside, gets compression all around For Avoiders: Open spaces only: No small, enclosed spaces Large areas: Provide very open, spacious areas for activities No confinement: Ensure child never feels trapped or confined
Massage Techniques: Full body compression massage: Firm pressure massage over entire body, simulating tight space compression, 10 minutes Wrap and massage: Wrap child loosely in blanket, massage through blanket, 5 minutes Joint compressions: Compress all major joints firmly, 5 seconds each, provides similar input to small spaces Manifestation 5: Standing on One Leg Frequently Physical Redirect Technique: Stand near child, join them balancing on one foot and say "Let's see how long we can balance." Count together to 30 seconds. Switch legs. Repeat 3 times per leg. Say "Great balance work! Now you can walk normally for 10 minutes." Set timer. DIY Alternative Tool: Balance Challenge System: Balance board: Make simple balance board from 2-foot board and half of pool noodle underneath, child practices balancing
Line walking: Use tape to create lines on floor (straight, curved, zigzag), child walks along them for balance practice Balance timer: Use timer - child balances on one foot for timed intervals (start 10 seconds, build to 60 seconds) Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Stair rail balance: Hold stair rail, practice standing on one foot 10 times per leg Pillow balance: Stand on couch cushion or pillow (on floor), balance on one foot - more challenging Heel-toe walking: Walk heel-to-toe in straight line across room, builds balance without one-leg standing Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: One-leg activities: Hop on one foot across room (10 hops each leg), kick ball with one foot repeatedly Yoga balance poses: Tree pose (standing on one leg), hold 30-60 seconds, both sides
Balance games: Simon Says with one-leg poses, freeze dance on one foot For Avoiders: Two-foot activities: All activities keep both feet on ground Supported balance: If must balance, hold onto something stable Seated activities: Prioritize sitting where balance isn't needed Massage Techniques: Ankle strengthening massage: Massage around ankle joints, 2 minutes each (ankles stabilize single-leg stance) Calf compression massage: Squeeze calf muscles firmly, 2 minutes each leg (work hard during balancing) Hip stabilizer massage: Massage outer hip and glute muscles, 2 minutes each side (stabilize pelvis when standing on one leg) Manifestation 6: Tucking Limbs Under Body When Sitting Physical Redirect Technique: Sit beside child, gently touch limb that's tucked and say "Let's check your legs/arms." Gently help them reposition limbs in comfortable but more typical position. Explain "Tucking can hurt your circulation - let's keep arms and legs free." Offer a lap pad or stuffed animal to hold instead.
DIY Alternative Tool: Position Reminder Tools: Lap buddy: Give child weighted stuffed animal (2-3 lbs) to hold in lap, occupies hands/arms Foot box: Place small box under desk/table, marked "feet go here" - gives feet a designated place Position photo: Take photo of child in good sitting position, place where they can see it as reminder Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Bean bag lap pad: Small bean bag (2-3 lbs) on lap provides weight without tucking limbs Armrest use: If chair has arms, teach child to rest arms on armrests properly Footstool: Provide footstool so feet have a comfortable place to rest Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Compression alternatives: Instead of tucking, provide compression through weighted lap pad, tight-fitting clothes Hand fidgets: Give stress ball or putty to occupy hands so they don't need to tuck
Stretching routine: Every 20 minutes, stretch all limbs fully extended, then return to proper sitting For Avoiders: Comfortable positions: Find most comfortable extended limb positions, maintain those Supportive furniture: Chair with proper arm and foot support so extended limbs are comfortable Cushion support: Add cushions under arms or feet for support Massage Techniques: Limb circulation massage: Massage arms and legs thoroughly to improve circulation (tucking restricts it), 2-3 minutes per limb Joint mobility massage: Massage and gently move each joint to maintain mobility, 1 minute per joint Extremity massage: Focus on hands and feet which get restricted when limbs are tucked, 2 minutes each Manifestation 7: Wrapping Legs Around Chair Legs Physical Redirect Technique: Kneel beside child, gently touch their wrapped leg and say "Let's unwrap your legs." Help them place feet flat on floor or footrest. Say "Feet belong on the floor. Let's find something else for your legs to do." Provide resistance band around chair legs for feet to push against.
DIY Alternative Tool: Foot/Leg Activity at Chair: Resistance band at chair: Tie exercise band or bungee around two front chair legs (stretched), child pushes feet against it Foot fidget box: Place small box with textured items under desk for feet to explore Footrest with texture: Use textured footrest (non-slip mat, rubber mat), gives feet something to do Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Tennis ball roll: Place tennis ball under desk, child rolls it under feet while sitting Bubble wrap mat: Small piece of bubble wrap under desk, child pops with feet (satisfying!) Textured rug: Place small textured rug under desk, feet rub against different textures Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Leg exercises at desk: Every 20 minutes, do 10 seated leg lifts per leg, 10 ankle rolls per ankle
Under-desk cycle: Small under-desk pedal exerciser, child pedals while sitting (provides leg input) Sitting leg squeezes: Squeeze ball or pillow between knees while sitting, 10 seconds, repeat 10 times For Avoiders: Proper footrest: Provide footrest at correct height, feet rest comfortably No leg activities: Keep legs still and relaxed, avoid fidgeting Comfortable position: Find one comfortable leg position and maintain it Massage Techniques: Leg unwinding massage: When unwrapping legs, massage them simultaneously, 2-3 minutes Circulation restoration: Firm massage from hip to ankle improving blood flow after legs were wrapped, 3 minutes each Ankle and calf: Focus on ankle and calf areas which wrap around chair legs, 2 minutes each Manifestation 8: Contorting Into Unusual Shapes Physical Redirect Technique: Approach carefully (unusual positions can be unstable), touch child's shoulder gently and say "Wow, you're very flexible! Let's try some yoga poses instead." Guide them into proper yoga pose (child's pose, downward dog, cat-cow) that provides similar body position sensation safely.
DIY Alternative Tool: Flexibility Activity Set: Yoga card deck: Make cards with stick figures showing different yoga poses, child draws card and does that pose Stretch routine chart: Poster showing 10-12 stretches, child works through routine when they have contorting urge Safe space for shapes: Designate yoga mat as place for unusual positions, only allowed there (contained and safe) Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Pillow props: Use pillows and cushions to support unusual positions safely Mirror practice: Child does positions in front of mirror, increases body awareness Stretch timer: Set timer for 30 seconds per unusual position, then must change to typical position Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Gymnastics/yoga class: Enroll in class teaching flexibility and body awareness properly Daily stretch routine: 10-15 minute stretch routine twice daily, satisfies positioning needs
Partner stretching: Adult helps child stretch safely, providing resistance and feedback For Avoiders: Typical positions only: Discourage unusual positioning Limited flexibility work: Minimal stretching, just basic gentle movements Stable positions: Encourage stable, typical body positions Massage Techniques: Full body flexibility massage: Massage combined with gentle stretching, all muscle groups, 10-15 minutes Joint mobility work: Gently move each joint through range of motion while massaging surrounding muscles Myofascial release: Hold sustained pressure on tight areas to release connective tissue, improve flexibility
Comprehensive Stimming Guide > 4. PROPRIOCEPTIVE STIMMING > B. Postural Stimming > Level 3: Sustained Positions
Causation: Over-stimulated: Sustained deep pressure is maximum calming Under-stimulated: Prolonged resistance provides lasting input Sensitivity: Craving continuous proprioceptive feedback Emotional: Sustained positions provide security and comfort Description: Maintaining difficult positions for extended periods Manifestation 1: Lying Under Weighted Blankets for Hours Physical Redirect Technique: Approach child under weighted blanket, gently touch through blanket and say "Time check - you've been under for X minutes. Let's take a break." Help them come out from under blanket. Have them stand, stretch, walk around for 5 minutes. Explain "Heavy blankets are good, but need breaks so body doesn't get too used to it." DIY Alternative Tool: Weighted Blanket Timer System: Use phone timer/alarm system Set intervals: 30 minutes under weighted blanket, 15 minutes out
Create chart: record time under blanket, ensure taking breaks Multiple blanket weights: have 2-3 different weights (light 5 lbs, medium 8 lbs, heavy 12 lbs), rotate weights to vary input Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Weighted breaks: Alternate weighted blanket with other proprioceptive inputs (carrying heavy items, push-ups, climbing stairs) Blanket fort: Under blanket is cozy but add books, activities so time has purpose beyond just pressure Scheduled blanket time: Designate specific times for weighted blanket (before bed, after school), not all day Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Alternative heavy input: Use compression vest, tight-fitting clothing, weighted lap pad during non-blanket times Physical activity: Before blanket time, do 15-20 minutes vigorous activity (running, jumping, climbing) Deep pressure alternatives: Body sock, compression squeeze, bear hugs throughout day
For Avoiders: Light blankets only: Very light blankets or regular blankets, no weight No long-term coverage: Brief blanket use only (10-15 minutes maximum) Open environment: Prefer uncovered, open feeling Massage Techniques: Matching massage to blanket: Deep, sustained pressure massage matching what weighted blanket provides, 10-15 minutes Full body compression: Compress all body parts firmly for 10 seconds each, similar to blanket weight Slow rhythmic massage: Slow, heavy strokes over entire body providing organizing input Manifestation 2: Staying in Tight Spaces (Closet, Boxes for 30-60+ minutes) Redirect Technique: Approach the tight space entrance, kneel down and speak softly "I see you're in your tight space. Let's set a timer. When it beeps, you need to come out and move around." Set timer for 20-30 minutes maximum. When timer sounds, insist they come out, move/stretch for 10 minutes before returning if desired.
DIY Alternative Tool: Tight Space Regulation: Space with timer: Place visible timer inside tight space, child can see when time to exit Music duration: Child can stay in tight space for duration of 2-3 songs, then must exit Activity-based: Only stay in space while doing specific activity (reading one book, completing one puzzle), then exit Comfort additions: Make space more purposeful - add reading light, books, quiet activities Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Rotating small spaces: Have 2-3 different approved tight spaces, rotate between them (prevents over-use of one) Purposeful use: Tight space is "reading cave" or "quiet thinking spot," not just compression space Exit rule: Child must be able to exit space immediately if asked - practice emergency exits Sensory Integration Activities:
For Seekers: Scheduled tight space time: Designate specific times (after school 30 min, before bed 20 min) for tight space use Alternative compression: Use body sock, compression clothing, weighted items when not in tight space Activity breaks: Between tight space sessions, do physical activities (running, jumping) 10-15 minutes For Avoiders: Open spaces only: No small or tight spaces Large, airy rooms: Prefer open, spacious environments No confinement: Avoid any enclosed or tight areas Massage Techniques: Post-space massage: After exiting tight space, full body massage to help transition, 5-10 minutes Circulation focus: Massage to improve circulation after being in cramped position, 5 minutes Stretching integration: Combine massage with gentle stretching after static positioning Manifestation 3: Maintaining Plank or Wall Sit Positions Excessively
Physical Redirect Technique: Approach child in position, kneel nearby and say "I'm impressed with your strength! Let's count together." Count to 30 seconds, then say "Time to rest - your muscles need a break." Insist they release position, rest for 2 minutes (can do gentle walking or stretching), then if desired, can repeat for another 30 seconds. Explain "Muscles grow during rest, not just during work." DIY Alternative Tool: Exercise Timer Protocol: Interval training: Use interval timer app (30 seconds work / 60 seconds rest) Rep counter: Track how many planks/wall sits completed rather than duration (5 reps of 20 seconds each = 100 seconds total but with breaks) Progressive chart: Chart showing safe durations (start 15 sec, add 5 sec per week up to max 60 sec per rep)
Form check video: Record child's form, watch together, emphasize quality over duration Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Multiple exercises: Instead of one exercise excessively, do circuit (20 sec plank, 20 sec wall sit, 20 sec push-ups, rest, repeat) Stability ball: Use stability ball for plank (hands on ball) or wall sit (ball behind back), adds challenge and variation Timer beeps: Phone timer beeps at 30 seconds, mandatory rest period Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Whole body workout: Channel the need for sustained positions into full workout routine (multiple exercises, proper rest between) Core routine: Structured core workout (planks, side planks, bridges, bird dogs) with rest periods, 10-15 minutes total Sports enrollment: Enroll in activity requiring sustained positions (martial arts, yoga, climbing) with proper instruction
For Avoiders: Gentle holds only: Very short duration holds (5-10 seconds maximum) Supported positions: Use props or support for any holding positions Minimal isometric work: Avoid sustained position holding Massage Techniques: Post-exercise massage: After plank/wall sits, massage core, arm, leg muscles used, 5-10 minutes Targeted muscle massage: Deep massage of specific muscles worked (abs, quads, shoulders), 2-3 minutes each Lactic acid release: Firm massage to help remove lactic acid build-up from sustained positions Manifestation 4: Staying Curled in Ball Position for Long Periods Physical Redirect Technique: Approach gently, touch child's back and say softly "You've been curled up for a while. Let's stretch like a cat." Guide them to come out of ball position, do cat-cow stretches (5 repetitions), then can return to ball if desired but only for 15 minutes (set timer).
DIY Alternative Tool: Ball Position Alternatives: Yoga ball: Child hugs large yoga ball to chest while sitting, similar to ball position but not as static Rocking chair: Sit in rocking chair with knees pulled up, rocking motion adds vestibular input to ball position Bean bag: Curl into bean bag chair, provides similar cocooning feeling but more adaptive Time tracking: Chart tracking duration in ball position, gradually working toward shorter periods Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Couch corner: Curl into corner of couch with cushions around, similar cozy feeling Blanket nest: Create nest of blankets and cushions, can curl into without being in pure ball position Recliner: Use recliner in tucked position, feet up, similar to ball but supported by furniture Sensory Integration Activities:
For Seekers: Yoga child's pose: Proper child's pose (knees wide, forehead to ground, arms extended) held for 2-3 minutes only Compression alternatives: Tight body sock, being wrapped in blanket, weighted blanket provide similar feeling Stretching routine: After curling, must do full body stretching routine (5-10 minutes) before recurling For Avoiders: Extended positions: Prefer stretched out, open body positions No curling: Avoid tucked or curled positions Open posture: Maintain open, relaxed body positions Massage Techniques: Spine mobilization massage: After being curled, massage along both sides of spine encouraging extension, 5 minutes Hip flexor release: Curling tightens hip flexors, massage front of hips, 2-3 minutes each Unfolding massage: As child extends from ball position, massage each body part as it unfolds Manifestation 5: Hanging from Bars Until Exhaustion
Physical Redirect Technique: Stand near child for safety, place hand near their back and say "I can see your arms are getting tired. Let's count to 10 together, then you drop down and rest." Count slowly. After release, have them shake out arms, stretch, rest for 3-5 minutes before hanging again. Explain "Strong muscles need rest time to rebuild." DIY Alternative Tool: Hanging Protocol System: Interval hanging: Use timer - hang 20 seconds, rest 60 seconds, repeat only 5 times per session Hang chart: Track hang times and number of hangs per day (limit 10-15 hangs total per day) Grip strength builder: Stress ball or grip strengthener to squeeze instead of hanging (alternative) Bar height adjustment: Lower bar so feet can touch ground during hang (takes some weight off arms)
Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Monkey bars: Playground monkey bars for shorter duration hanging (moving across rather than static hanging) Towel hang: Drape towel over bar, hold towel ends (easier on hands than bare bar) Supported hang: Bar low enough that feet touch ground, supports some weight Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Upper body strength circuit: Instead of just hanging, circuit of pull-ups, hangs, arm exercises with rest periods Climbing activities: Rock climbing, rope climbing (at gym), tree climbing provide hanging input with movement Swimming: Arm strokes in swimming provide similar muscle work without sustained hanging For Avoiders: No hanging: Avoid hanging activities entirely Supported upper body work: Upper body exercises while seated or supported Light arm activities: Gentle arm movements without hanging or weight-bearing
Massage Techniques: Shoulder decompression massage: After hanging, massage shoulders while gently pulling arms to decompress joints, 3-5 minutes Forearm and hand deep massage: Hanging stresses these areas, deep massage, 3-5 minutes Upper back release: Massage upper back and shoulder blades thoroughly after hanging, 5 minutes Manifestation 6: Staying in Child's Pose or Fetal Position Extensively Physical Redirect Technique: Approach child in position, kneel nearby and say gently "I see you need to curl up and rest. Let's make sure your body stays healthy." Set timer for 15-20 minutes. When timer sounds, guide them through gentle spinal stretches (cat-cow, gentle twists) for 3-5 minutes before allowing return to position if desired. DIY Alternative Tool: Position Rotation System: Yoga sequence: Create sequence - child's pose (5 min), cobra pose (1 min), child's pose (5 min), downward dog (1 min), repeat
Position timer: Visual timer showing when to switch from curled to extended position Activity in position: While in position, listen to audio book, music (gives position purpose beyond just compression) Bolster support: Use yoga bolster or rolled blankets under chest during child's pose, makes it more comfortable for longer hold Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Couch fetal position: Curl into fetal position on couch instead of floor (more comfortable for extended time) Pillow support: Place pillows under and around body in fetal position for additional support and comfort Recliner option: Recliner in tucked position provides similar cocooning with better support Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Compression alternatives: When not in fetal position, use weighted blanket, body sock, compression vest Yoga practice: Structured yoga practice moving through various poses including child's pose (but not staying excessively)
Heavy work before curling: Do 10-15 minutes heavy work (push-ups, carrying, climbing) before curling, satisfies sensory need For Avoiders: Open positions: Prefer relaxed, extended body positions No prolonged curling: Avoid sustained fetal or child's pose positions Supported sitting: Comfortable supported sitting rather than curling Massage Techniques: Spinal release massage: Massage entire length of spine encouraging healthy movement, 5-7 minutes Hip and lower back focus: These areas compress in fetal position, massage thoroughly, 5 minutes Full body extension massage: Massage while gently encouraging body to extend from curled position Manifestation 7: Prolonged Pressure-Seeking (Being "Sandwiched") between objects Physical Redirect Technique: Approach the "sandwich" situation, carefully remove one layer and say "You've had good pressure for X minutes. Time for a pressure break." Help child completely exit sandwich. Have them stand, walk, do 5 jumping jacks, stretch. Rest 10 minutes before allowing return to pressure if desired. Set timer for next pressure session (20-30 minutes maximum).
DIY Alternative Tool: Sandwich Schedule System: Pressure intervals: 20 minutes sandwiched, 15 minutes free movement, repeat only 2-3 times per day Pressure alternatives: Rotate between being sandwiched, wearing weighted vest, tight clothing, bear hugs Emergency exit: Always ensure child can exit sandwich immediately if needed (practice this) Chart tracking: Log duration and frequency of pressure-seeking, gradually work toward less time Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Varied pressure sources: Instead of prolonged sandwich, rotate through: weighted blanket 10 min, tight hug 2 min, compression vest 15 min, body sock 10 min Active pressure: Give pressure during movement activities (weighted backpack while walking) rather than static sandwich Furniture sandwich: Use couch back and heavy cushions (safer than makeshift sandwiches) Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers:
Scheduled deep pressure: Set specific times for deep pressure activities (morning, after school, before bed) rather than continuous Heavy work substitution: Every other pressure session, substitute heavy work activities (push-ups, carrying, climbing) 15-20 minutes Compression clothing: Wear compression clothing throughout day providing ongoing light pressure For Avoiders: No deep pressure: Avoid all sandwich or compression activities Light touch only: If any touch, very light and brief Open space preference: Maintain personal space without pressure or compression Massage Techniques: Deep compression massage: Provide deep pressure massage matching sandwich pressure but safer, 10-15 minutes Sequential compression: Compress each body part individually for 10 seconds, provides similar input to sandwich Heavy rolling massage: Use therapy ball or rolling pin with firm pressure over entire body, 10 minutes
SENSORY DIET PROTOCOL What is a Sensory Diet? A sensory diet is a customized schedule of physical activities and sensory experiences designed throughout the day to help a child stay focused, organized, and calm. Like nutritional food needs, children need a balanced "diet" of sensory input. This protocol helps parents plan appropriate sensory activities. General Principles 1. Consistency is Key Implement sensory activities at the SAME TIMES daily Predictable routines help nervous system organization Build sensory activities into existing routines 2. Intensity and Duration Start with 5-10 minute sessions Gradually increase as tolerated High-intensity input (jumping, crashing) = 10-15 minutes Calming input (massage, deep pressure) = 15-20 minutes 3. Timing Morning: Alerting/organizing activities (jumping, resistive work) Midday: Re-organizing activities (movement breaks, heavy work)
Before difficult tasks: Calming/organizing activities Evening: Calming activities (massage, compression, quiet time) 4. Signs Child Needs Sensory Break Fidgeting, restlessness, inability to sit still Excessive stimming behaviors increasing Difficulty focusing or following directions Emotional dysregulation (meltdowns, tantrums, irritability) Seeking out intense sensory experiences 5. "Sensory Snacks" Quick 2-3 minute sensory inputs between main activities Examples: 10 chair push-ups, wall pushes, quick squeeze of stress ball Use whenever child seems dysregulated Scheduled deep pressure: Set specific times for deep pressure activities (morning, after school, before bed) rather than continuous Heavy work substitution: Every other pressure session, substitute heavy work activities (push-ups, carrying, climbing) 15-20 minutes Compression clothing: Wear compression clothing throughout day providing ongoing light pressure For Avoiders: No deep pressure: Avoid all sandwich or compression activities
Light touch only: If any touch, very light and brief Open space preference: Maintain personal space without pressure or compression Massage Techniques: Deep compression massage: Provide deep pressure massage matching sandwich pressure but safer, 10-15 minutes Sequential compression: Compress each body part individually for 10 seconds, provides similar input to sandwich Heavy rolling massage: Use therapy ball or rolling pin with firm pressure over entire body, 10 minutes SENSORY DIET PROTOCOL What is a Sensory Diet? A sensory diet is a customized schedule of physical activities and sensory experiences designed throughout the day to help a child stay focused, organized, and calm. Like nutritional food needs, children need a balanced "diet" of sensory input. This protocol helps parents plan appropriate sensory activities.
General Principles 1. Consistency is Key Implement sensory activities at the SAME TIMES daily Predictable routines help nervous system organization Build sensory activities into existing routines 2. Intensity and Duration Start with 5-10 minute sessions Gradually increase as tolerated High-intensity input (jumping, curashing) = 10-15 minutes Calming input (massage, deep pressure) = 15-20 minutes 3. Timing Morning: Alerting/organizing activities (jumping, resistive work) Midday: Re-organizing activities (movement breaks, heavy work) Before difficult tasks: Calming/organizing activities Evening: Calming activities (massage, compression, quiet time) 4. Signs Child Needs Sensory Break Fidgeting, restlessness, inability to sit still Excessive stimming behaviors increasing Difficulty focusing or following directions Emotional dysregulation (meltdowns, tantrums, irritability) Seeking out intense sensory experiences 5. "Sensory Snacks" Quick 2-3 minute sensory inputs between main activities
Examples: 10 chair push-ups, wall pushes, quick squeeze of stress ball Use whenever child seems dysregulated SENSORY DIET PLANNING TABLE This table helps you plan a daily sensory diet based on your child's specific proprioceptive stim behaviors. Find your child's main behaviors in the left column, then use the suggested activities in the right columns for different times of day. SAMPLE DAILY SENSORY DIET SCHEDULE For a child exhibiting multiple proprioceptive stim behaviors (pressing, heavy work, position changes) 6:30 AM - WAKE UP ROUTINE Alerting input: Jump on trampoline 5 minutes OR jump on bed 20 jumps Heavy work: Carry stack of books to another room and back (3 trips) Organizing: Wall push-ups 10 repetitions 7:30 AM - BEFORE SCHOOL Calming: Compression massage 5 minutes OR tight hug 30 seconds
Weighted backpack (2-3 lbs) worn for 10 minutes during breakfast prep 10:00 AM - SCHOOL BREAK (if possible) Movement: Run/walk around playground 5 minutes Heavy work: Carry classroom supplies, push furniture Sensory snack: Squeeze stress ball 30 times 12:00 PM - LUNCHTIME Before eating: Chair push-ups 5 repetitions During lunch: Sit on wobble cushion After eating: Walk while carrying lunch box/backpack 2:00 PM - AFTERNOON TRANSITION Re-energizing: Jump on trampoline 5 minutes OR jumping jacks 30 reps Heavy work: Push/pull heavy item 10 feet and back Organizing: Plank hold 20 seconds 3:30 PM - AFTER SCHOOL Major sensory input time: Choose 2-3 activities Playground climbing 15 minutes Weighted vest wearing while doing chores 20 minutes Rough play/pillow wrestling 10 minutes Swimming, sports practice, or running 20-30 minutes
5:00 PM - BEFORE HOMEWORK Heavy work: Carry groceries, take out trash, vacuum room Calming: Deep pressure massage 10 minutes Organizing: Wall pushes 10 repetitions, then settle to homework with wobble cushion 5:30 PM - DURING HOMEWORK Sensory snacks every 15-20 minutes: Stand and do 5 squats Squeeze stress ball 20 times Chair push-ups 5 repetitions 6:30 PM - BEFORE DINNER Moderately alerting: Help set table (carrying items), help cook (stirring, mixing) Position variety: Stand at counter to help with prep 8:00 PM - BEFORE BED ROUTINE Calming sequence (very important): Heavy work: Push furniture back into place, carry laundry Deep pressure: 15-minute massage focusing on arms, legs, back Compression: Burrito roll in blanket 5 minutes Weighted blanket: Use during bedtime story
Sustained position: Child's pose or fetal position 3-5 minutes 8:30 PM - BEDTIME Weighted blanket on bed (should be ~10% of child's body weight) Compression sheet or sleeping bag if preferred Body sock if child requests SIMPLIFIED SENSORY DIET CHECKLIST Print this checklist and check off activities as completed each day: MORNING (Choose 2-3): □ Jumping/bouncing activity (5 min) □ Heavy carrying (3-5 trips) □ Push-ups or wall pushes (10 reps) □ Climbing or stair climbing □ Rough play or wrestling (5 min) MIDDAY (Choose 2): □ Movement break (run, jump, climb - 5 min) □ Heavy work chore □ Resistance or pulling activity □ Position changes or exercises BEFORE DIFFICULT TASKS (Choose 1-2): □ Chair push-ups (5 reps) □ Quick massage or compression (2-3 min)
□ Wall pushes (10 reps) □ Squeeze stress ball (20-30 times) EVENING (Choose 2-3): □ Heavy work activities (15 min) □ Deep pressure massage (10-15 min) □ Weighted blanket or vest □ Calming stretches or yoga □ Compression or tight spaces (15-20 min) THROUGHOUT DAY (As Needed): □ Wobble cushion during seated work □ Fidget tools available □ Movement breaks every 20-30 minutes □ Heavy work tasks assigned TROUBLESHOOTING YOUR SENSORY DIET "My child seems MORE hyper after sensory activities" You may be providing too much alerting input Switch to calming activities (deep pressure, slow movements) Reduce intensity and duration Ensure activities end with calming component "My child doesn't want to do the activities" Make activities fun and game-like Let child choose between 2-3 options
Use rewards/motivation systems Join in the activities yourself Break activities into smaller increments "I don't have time for all these activities" Start with just 3 key times: morning, after school, before bed Combine sensory activities with necessary tasks (heavy work = chores) Use quick "sensory snacks" (2-3 minutes) instead of longer sessions Build sensory input into existing routines "The behaviors are getting worse, not better" May need more intense or more frequent sensory input May need different types of activities - try variety Consult with occupational therapist for assessment Keep log of what works and what doesn't Be patient - takes 2-4 weeks to see changes "How do I know if it's working?" Child can focus better on tasks Stimming behaviors decrease in frequency
Child appears more organized and calm Fewer meltdowns and emotional dysregulation Child requests sensory activities when feeling dysregulated Improved sleep patterns EMERGENCY REGULATION STRATEGIES When child is completely dysregulated (meltdown, extreme stimming): Immediate deep pressure (choose one): Bear hug (firm, 30-60 seconds) Weighted blanket immediately Compression between cushions Tight body sock Heavy work (choose one): Wall push-ups 20 repetitions Push heavy furniture across room Carry very heavy items Climb stairs rapidly 3-5 times Rhythmic movement: Rocking in rocking chair Swinging (if available) Bouncing on therapy ball Safe space: Allow retreat to quiet, dim space Provide compression options Limit demands temporarily Recovery: Deep pressure massage 10-15 minutes Calm, quiet activities Gradual reintegration to demands
Comprehensive Stimming Guide > 5. VESTIBULAR STIMMING
(Balance, Movement, and Spatial Orientation)
Comprehensive Stimming Guide > 5. VESTIBULAR STIMMING > A. Linear Movement Stimming > Level 1: Rocking
Causation: Over-stimulated: Rhythmic movement is organizing and calming Under-stimulated: Vestibular system needs movement input Sensitivity: Self-soothing mechanism; regulates arousal level Developmental: May persist from infant self-soothing patterns Emotional: Increases during anxiety, excitement, or processing Sensory Profile: Seeker: Fast, intense rocking for extended periods Avoider: Slow, gentle rocking to self-soothe in overwhelming environments Mixed: Moderate rocking while processing information or emotions Description: Rhythmic back-and-forth or side-to-side movement Manifestation 1: Rocking While Sitting (Front-Back or Side-Side, 20-200+rocks) Physical Redirect Technique: Approach child calmly from the side, place hand gently on their shoulder and say "I see you're rocking. Let's rock together properly." Sit beside them, establish eye contact, and rock together for 10 slow, controlled rocks counting aloud. Then say "Now let's try sitting still for 5 minutes" and set a visible timer.
DIY Alternative Tool: Rocking Cushion: Take a 2-liter plastic bottle, fill halfway with water, cap tightly. Place bottle on its side on chair, put firm cushion on top. Child sits on cushion which rocks gently with any movement. Or cut a pool noodle in half lengthwise, tape under seat cushion to create gentle rocking base. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Rocking chair: Provide actual rocking chair for structured rocking times (15 minutes morning and evening) Exercise ball sitting: Use properly-sized therapy/exercise ball as chair - allows natural rocking while sitting Cushion with marbles: Fill gallon ziplock bag with 2 cups dried beans or marbles, place under regular cushion, creates subtle movement when sitting Metronome app: Download free metronome app, set to 60-80 bpm, child rocks in rhythm to beats (makes rocking more organized)
Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Scheduled rocking time: 10-15 minute rocking sessions 3x daily on rocking chair or therapy ball Rocking boat pose: Yoga pose - lie on stomach, lift arms and legs, rock back and forth on belly 20 times Hammock time: If possible, install indoor hammock or use outdoor one, 20-30 minutes daily with rocking motion Platform swing: Create platform swing (board suspended by 4 ropes), child sits and rocks on it 15-20 minutes For Avoiders: Stable seating only: Very stable chair with no movement Back support: High-backed chair with armrests for maximum stability Feet grounded: Ensure feet flat on floor or footrest, very grounding Minimal movement: Avoid any rocking activities Massage Techniques: Slow rhythmic back massage: Massage back in slow, rhythmic strokes matching rocking rhythm, 5-10 minutes - very organizing
Vestibular calming massage: Massage base of skull where it meets neck (sub-occipital area) with gentle circular pressure, 2-3 minutes Full body linear strokes: Long, slow strokes from head to toe following body's midline, 10 minutes, mimics rocking sensation Vestibular Integration: Linear vestibular input: Before seated activities, provide linear movement (swinging forward-back on swing 5 minutes, scooter board rides) Proprioceptive grounding: After rocking, do 10 wall push-ups and 10 squats to ground nervous system Visual calming: Dim lights during rocking activities, reduces visual stimulation allowing vestibular focus Manifestation 2: Rocking While Standing (Shifting Weight Rhythmically) Physical Redirect Technique: Stand facing child, make eye contact and say "Let's practice strong standing." Place your hands on their shoulders (light touch), guide them to plant feet firmly hip-width apart. Have them push down through feet, hold for 10 seconds, release. Repeat 5 times. Say "Feel your strong, steady feet."
DIY Alternative Tool: Balance Board: Make simple balance board from piece of plywood (18"x12") and half of a pool noodle underneath (tape securely). Child stands on board which allows controlled rocking. Or use a thick folded towel under feet creating slight instability that satisfies rocking need. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Standing desk with wobble board: Use counter-height surface for activities, child stands on cushion or folded blanket allowing subtle weight shifting Foot rocker: Use thick book or small box under toes or heels (alternating), allows controlled rocking while standing Wall lean: Child stands leaning against wall (touching shoulder blades), can rock side-to-side safely against wall support Standing on one foot practice: Alternate standing on each foot for 30 seconds, provides movement while building balance
Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Active standing tasks: While standing, do activities requiring movement (throwing ball at target, reaching up/down for items) Trampoline standing: Stand on mini trampoline (3-4 ft diameter), can bounce gently or just stand with subtle movement Balance beam walking: Use 2x4 board on ground, walk back and forth 10 times Yoga balance poses: Tree pose, warrior poses held for 30-60 seconds each For Avoiders: Seated activities: Avoid standing activities when possible Wide stable stance: If must stand, feet wide apart for maximum stability Supported standing: Always near wall or furniture to hold onto Short standing periods: Only 5-10 minutes standing maximum Massage Techniques: Leg grounding massage: Firm downward strokes from hip to ankle, 2 minutes per leg, helps child feel "rooted"
Foot pressure massage: Deep pressure on soles of feet, 2-3 minutes each, increases proprioceptive awareness of ground Ankle circles with compression: Hold ankle, rotate foot in circles while providing gentle compression, 10 circles each direction per foot Vestibular Integration: Proprioceptive heavy work before standing: 5 minutes of heavy work (carrying, pushing) before expected standing periods Visual focus point: During standing, have child focus eyes on one stable point, reduces vestibular input need Alternate standing/sitting: Switch positions every 15 minutes rather than prolonged standing Manifestation 3: Rocking in Bed Before Sleep (30-120 minutes) Physical Redirect Technique: Enter room calmly during rocking, sit on edge of bed and place hand on child's leg. Say softly "Your body wants to rock to feel sleepy. Let's try a better way." Guide them to lie still while you gently rock/pat them rhythmically for 2-3 minutes, gradually slowing the rhythm until stopping. Alternatively, rock their legs side-to-side slowly.
DIY Alternative Tool: Bed Hammock Effect: Thread a long resistance band or stretchy fabric under the mattress and secure on both sides of bed frame, creating slight suspended feeling. Or place pool noodle sections under mattress corners creating gentle rocking when child moves. Rocking Bed Solution: Place bed on carpet with smooth furniture sliders under bed legs - allows subtle rocking. Or partially deflate air mattress creating more give and subtle movement response. Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Body pillow: Large body pillow placed lengthwise in bed, child hugs it or drapes leg over it, provides compression reducing rocking need Weighted blanket: Use weighted blanket (10% of child's body weight), deep pressure reduces rocking urge Bed wedge: Use pillows to create slight incline (head higher), changes vestibular input reducing rocking need
Rhythmic music: Play slow, rhythmic music (60 bpm) or white noise with heartbeat rhythm, provides auditory rhythm replacing rocking Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Pre-bed vestibular input: 15 minutes before bed - jumping on trampoline 5 min, spinning in office chair 2 min, rocking in rocking chair 8 min Vigorous activity 2 hours before bed: Run, climb, jump for 30+ minutes earlier in evening to satisfy vestibular needs Bedtime routine with movement: Bath (water provides vestibular input), then gentle yoga stretches, then reading in rocking chair Hammock bed alternative: If possible, sleep in hammock or suspended bed legitimizing rocking need For Avoiders: Very stable bed: Ensure bed doesn't move or rock at all Grounding routine: Before bed, massage feet firmly, do heavy work (push-ups against bed)
