Predictable routine: Same exact bedtime sequence every night, very calming Minimal movement: Avoid any movement activities before bed Massage Techniques: Slow rhythmic bedtime massage: 15-20 minute massage with slow, rhythmic strokes matching rocking rhythm, 60-80 strokes per minute Head-to-toe massage sequence: Start at scalp, massage down entire body to feet with consistent pressure and rhythm Joint compressions: Compress each major joint for 10 seconds (shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles) - very calming and organizing Vestibular Integration: Vestibular sensory diet before bed: Structured movement activities 30-60 minutes before sleep (see sensory diet section) Proprioceptive loading: Heavy work immediately before bed (push bed against wall 10 times, carry heavy laundry basket) Gradual transition: 30 min calm activities → 15 min quieter → 10 min massage → sleep
Manifestation 4: Rocking While Holding Objects or People Physical Redirect Technique: Approach gently, place hand on child's arm and say "I see you need to rock with [object/person]. Let's rock safely together." If holding person, establish appropriate rocking parameters (how hard, how long). If holding object, ensure object is safe to rock with. Guide them through 20 controlled rocks, then transition to stillness with deep pressure (hug if person, weighted lap if alone). DIY Alternative Tool: Weighted Rocking Object: Create weighted stuffed animal by filling old stuffed toy with rice or poly pellets (2-4 lbs), sew closed. Child holds this while rocking in rocking chair - combines weight and rocking. Or fill backpack with books (5-10 lbs), child wears while rocking in chair.
Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Large therapy ball: Child sits on floor hugging large therapy ball, rocks back and forth hugging ball Pillow rocking: Stack 2-3 firm pillows, child lays on top and rocks, pillows provide comfort and slight instability Resistance band rocking: Loop resistance band around something stable (table leg), hold other end while rocking - band provides resistance feedback Parent-child rocking: Designated rocking time - parent and child rock together in rocking chair or on floor 10-15 minutes Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Rocking with purpose: Rock while reading, listening to audiobook, watching calm show - makes rocking functional Weighted vest rocking: Wear weighted vest while rocking in rocking chair, 15-20 minutes Platform swing hugging pillow: On platform swing, child hugs heavy pillow while swinging/rocking
Partner rocking: Two people sit back-to-back on floor, rock together side-to-side (provides proprioceptive input plus rocking) For Avoiders: Stationary holding: Hold objects or people while sitting completely still Grounded positions: Ensure feet flat on floor, body well-supported Brief durations: Any rocking limited to 2-3 minutes maximum Supported positions: Always use chair or furniture support Massage Techniques: Massage while rocking: Provide massage simultaneously with rocking (massage back while sitting on therapy ball rocking) Arms and hands: Massage arms and hands that are holding objects, 3-5 minutes, helps release tension Shoulder and neck release: Holding while rocking creates shoulder tension, massage these areas thoroughly 5 minutes Vestibular Integration: Weighted input while rocking: Always combine rocking with proprioceptive input (weighted lap pad, compression vest)
Bilateral integration: Rock while tossing ball hand to hand, or doing hand movements - integrates both brain sides Transition protocol: Rock 5 minutes → slow down gradually 2 minutes → stop with deep pressure 3 minutes Manifestation 5: Rocking During Stress or Concentration Physical Redirect Technique: When you observe stress-related rocking, approach calmly and say "I notice you're rocking because [situation]. Let's do something that helps even more." Offer immediate alternative: quick walk around room, 10 jumping jacks, stress ball squeezing, or brief rocking in designated rocking chair. After 2-3 minutes alternative, return to stressful task with support. DIY Alternative Tool: Desk Wobble System: Under-desk foot rocker: Place thick paperback book or small box under desk, child rocks feet on it while sitting
Seat disk: Partially inflated beach ball in pillowcase under bottom on chair, allows rocking while appearing to sit still Resistance band on chair: Tie exercise band around front chair legs, child pushes feet against it rhythmically Stress rocking timer: Use visual timer - when stressed, allowed 3 minutes of rocking in rocking chair, then return to task Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Gum chewing: During stressful/concentration tasks, allow gum chewing (rhythmic jaw movement substitutes for rocking) Foot fidget: Tennis ball or foot roller under desk, rock/roll feet on it during stress Hand fidgets: Stress ball, therapy putty, or smooth stone to squeeze/manipulate during concentration Music with rhythm: Instrumental music with steady beat (60-80 bpm) through headphones, provides auditory rhythm Sensory Integration Activities:
For Seekers: Pre-stress heavy work: Before known stressful tasks, 10 minutes heavy work (wall push-ups, carrying heavy items, stair climbing) Movement breaks: Every 15-20 minutes during concentration tasks, 2-minute movement break (run in place, jump, spin) Compression during tasks: Wear weighted vest or compression vest during stressful activities Chew tool: Use chewable jewelry or chew tool during concentration tasks For Avoiders: Stable environment: Very stable, predictable environment during stressful times Grounding techniques: Focus on feet on floor, hands on desk - physical grounding Minimal movement: Reduce all movement requirements during stress Supported seating: Very stable, supportive chair with armrests and back support Massage Techniques: Quick calming massage: 3-5 minute massage break during stressful tasks (shoulders, hands, scalp) Self-massage techniques: Teach child to massage own temples, hands, neck during stress (empowering)
Pressure points: Firm pressure on specific calming points (between thumb/index finger webbing, center of palm) for 30 seconds Vestibular Integration: Proprioceptive instead of vestibular: During concentration, proprioceptive input (weighted lap pad, foot pressure on floor) may work better than vestibular Visual focus: During stressful tasks, reduce visual clutter, focus on one area - reduces overall sensory load Breathing with rhythm: Teach rhythmic breathing (4 counts in, 4 counts out) - provides internal rhythm replacing rocking Manifestation 6: Gentle Swaying While Standing Still Physical Redirect Technique: Stand beside child, mirror their swaying briefly, then say "Let's stand strong and tall." Place hands on their shoulders, guide them to find center of gravity (equal weight on both feet). Have them imagine roots growing from feet into floor. Hold stable position 30 seconds, release, repeat 3 times. Praise stability.
DIY Alternative Tool: Standing Balance Tool: Yoga mat with texture: Place textured yoga mat or bath mat where child stands, provides tactile feedback to feet reducing sway need Footprints on floor: Use colored tape to create footprint outlines on floor, child stands with feet in footprints (visual cue for stability) Balance pod: Fill gallon ziplock bag with rice, seal well, tape to floor, child stands on it (allows tiny movements satisfying sway need) Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Lean posts: When standing in one place (waiting, in line), have child lean on one leg then the other, shifting weight (controlled sway) Foot exercises while standing: While standing, do ankle rolls, toe raises, heel raises - provides movement outlet Standing balance games: Balance small beanbag on head while standing, stand on one foot for time challenges
Wall support: Stand with back against wall, can sway slightly against wall support Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Trampoline standing: When need to stand still, allow standing on mini trampoline with subtle bouncing Fidget tools: Hand fidgets while standing (stress ball, fidget spinner) - redirects movement need to hands Standing movement breaks: Every 10 minutes of standing, 1 minute of movement (march in place, jump 10 times) Shifting base: Instead of standing flat-footed, stand on toes then heels alternating - purposeful movement For Avoiders: Sitting instead: Provide seating whenever possible instead of standing Short standing periods: Only stand for 5-10 minutes before sitting break Stable support: Always near wall or furniture to hold if needed Wide stance: Feet shoulder-width or wider for maximum stability
Massage Techniques: Leg and hip massage: Massage legs and hips before standing activities, 5 minutes, improves position sense Foot reflexology: Firm massage of entire foot sole, 2-3 minutes each foot, grounding Calf stretching massage: Massage calves while gently stretching, helps with standing stability Vestibular Integration: Visual reference point: When standing, focus eyes on stable visual target (picture on wall, specific object) Proprioceptive loading: Heavy work before standing periods (carry heavy bag, push against wall) Balance training: Daily balance exercises (stand on one foot, walk heel-to-toe line) improve standing stability Manifestation 7: Head Rocking Independently from Body Physical Redirect Technique: Approach from front, establish eye contact, place hands gently on sides of child's head (not restricting, just providing sensory input) and say "Let's keep your head still and strong." Hold steady gentle pressure for 10 seconds. Then guide through controlled head movements: 5 slow "yes" nods, 5 slow "no" shakes, 5 ear-to-shoulder tilts each side. Then practice holding head still for 30 seconds.
DIY Alternative Tool: Head Stabilization Tools: Soft neck support: Roll small hand towel, wrap around neck like scarf (not tight), provides proprioceptive input to neck reducing rocking urge Weighted headband: Sew small beads or fishing weights into fabric headband (1-2 oz total), child wears during activities, provides head awareness Balance beanbag: Child balances small beanbag on head during activities, encourages head stillness Head position timer: Use timer - hold head still for increasing intervals (start 30 seconds, build to 5 minutes) Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Neck exercises: Structured neck stretches - 10 reps each direction (up/down, side/side, ear-to-shoulder) Cold compress on neck: Wrap cold pack (or frozen peas) in towel, place on back of neck 3-5 minutes - provides strong sensory input
Chin tucks: Press chin back toward neck (making double chin), hold 5 seconds, repeat 10 times - proprioceptive input to neck Head massage while still: Massage scalp and base of skull while child keeps head still, 5 minutes Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Vigorous head-moving activities: Before need for stillness, do activities legitimizing head movement (headbanging to music, head shaking games, nodding "yes" 100 times) Vestibular input through body: Satisfy vestibular needs through whole body movement (spinning, swinging) reducing isolated head movement need Neck strengthening: Exercises strengthening neck muscles (resist hand pressure on head from all directions, 10 reps each) Balance challenges: Activities requiring head stability (walk with book on head, balance board standing) For Avoiders: Supported head positions: Use pillows, headrest, or furniture to support head
Minimal head movement: Avoid activities requiring head turning or tilting Stable visual field: Keep head still, move eyes only when scanning environment Gentle stretches only: Very gentle, slow neck stretches, no sudden movements Massage Techniques: Sub-occipital release: Massage the base of skull where it meets neck with gentle circular pressure, 3-5 minutes - releases tension and calms vestibular system Neck and shoulder massage: Full neck and shoulder massage, 10 minutes, releases tension from head rocking Scalp massage: Firm pressure scalp massage with fingertips, 5 minutes, very organizing for vestibular system Jaw massage: Massage jaw muscles (often tight with head rocking), 2-3 minutes each side Vestibular Integration: Whole body vestibular input: Provide full-body vestibular activities reducing need for isolated head movement Proprioceptive neck input: Joint compressions to neck (gentle downward pressure on top of head, child resists) 10 reps
Visual stability exercises: Focus eyes on one point while moving head slightly - integrates visual-vestibular systems Manifestation 8: Rocking at Specific Speeds/Rhythms (Consistent BPM) Physical Redirect Technique: Observe and match the child's rocking rhythm. Approach, sit beside them, and rock with them for 10 rocks. Then say "Let's change our rhythm." Use a metronome app (free download) to establish new rhythm - start with their preferred BPM, then gradually slow it by 10 BPM increments over 2-3 minutes until reaching calmer 60 BPM. Rock together to the new rhythm. DIY Alternative Tool: Rhythm Control System: Metronome app: Free smartphone app, set to specific BPMs, child rocks to beat, you control speed Music playlist by BPM: Create playlists at different BPMs (120, 100, 80, 60), use to regulate rocking speed
Visual rhythm cue: Create flashcard with dot moving back and forth at desired speed (pendulum app or video), child matches rhythm Rocking chair with timer: Rocking chair plus visual timer - rock at certain speed for set time, then transition to different activity Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Rhythmic activities: Substitute rocking with other rhythmic activities at specific BPM - bouncing ball, drumming, marching Bilateral activities: Activities using both sides of body rhythmically - clapping patterns, bilateral ball tossing, patting knees alternately Heartbeat focus: Place hand on heart, try to rock at heartbeat rhythm (usually 60-80 BPM), connects to internal rhythm Rhythm instruments: Simple instruments (drum, shakers) allow rhythmic expression without full body rocking Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Structured rhythm sessions: 10-15 minute sessions 3x daily - rock to metronome, gradually change speeds, practice different rhythms
Musical activities: Drumming, dancing, playing instruments satisfy rhythm needs Bilateral coordination: Activities requiring rhythmic bilateral movement (swimming strokes, jumping jacks to beat) Rhythmic sports: Activities with rhythm (jump rope, dribbling basketball, running to music) For Avoiders: No forced rhythm: Avoid rhythmic activities if uncomfortable Self-paced activities: Child controls rhythm and speed Calm, slow rhythms only: If any rhythm, very slow (60 BPM or less) Predictable patterns: Same rhythm every time if engaging in rhythmic activities Massage Techniques: Rhythmic massage: Massage at specific BPM matching child's preferred rhythm initially, gradually slow rhythm during massage session Bilateral massage: Massage both sides of body simultaneously in rhythm (both arms at once, both legs at once) Tapping massage: Instead of stroking, use rhythmic tapping (tapotement technique) at consistent BPM, 5-10 minutes
Vestibular Integration: Metronome training: Use metronome during various activities teaching nervous system to entrain to different rhythms Rhythm variability practice: Practice rocking at many different speeds, increases flexibility Calming rhythm transition: Always end rocking sessions with slow 60 BPM rhythm before stopping - aids transition to stillness
Comprehensive Stimming Guide > 5. VESTIBULAR STIMMING > A. Linear Movement Stimming > Level 2: Bouncing and Jumping
Causation: Over-stimulated: Impact/landing provides organizing input to nervous system Under-stimulated: Craves intense vestibular stimulation from acceleration/deceleration Sensitivity: Under-responsive vestibular system needs strong input Regulation: Bouncing modulates arousal (can calm OR alert) Proprioceptive: Combines vestibular + joint compression from landing Sensory Profile: Extreme Seeker: Hours of jumping; high intensity; seeks maximum height Impact Seeker: Focuses on landing sensation; heavy landings Fidgety: Constant small bounces; can't stay still Description: Vertical movement patterns Manifestation 1: Bouncing on Toes While Standing (100-500+ bounces daily) Physical Redirect Technique: Approach child, place hands on their shoulders and say "Let's bounce properly." Guide them to do 20 controlled, full bounces (bending knees, full body bounce, not just toes). Count together. Then say "Now let's feel strong flat feet" - have them plant feet flat, press down through heels, hold for 10 seconds. Repeat: 20 bounces, 10 second flat-feet hold, 3 times total.
DIY Alternative Tool: Controlled Bouncing Station: Mini trampoline: Small 3-4 foot trampoline for safe, contained bouncing (can find at discount stores for $20-30) Cushioned bounce spot: Stack 3-4 thick couch cushions, tape together, designated "bounce spot" for toe bouncing Resistance band for feet: Loop resistance band around ankles, bouncing works against resistance providing more input Bounce tracker: Use counter app or tally marks - track bounces, set daily limit (250 bounces), child monitors own bouncing Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Calf raises: Instead of bouncing, do 20 structured calf raises (up on toes, hold 3 seconds, lower) - same muscle work Stair step bouncing: Stand on bottom stair, bounce/step up and down 30 times Jump rope: Jump rope provides structured bouncing with activity purpose, 5-10 minutes
Pogo stick: If age-appropriate, pogo stick provides intense bouncing input Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Scheduled bouncing: 10-minute bouncing sessions 3x daily on trampoline or designated spot Jumping activities: Jump rope, jumping jacks, jump-up-and-down games throughout day Trampoline park visits: Weekly visit to trampoline park for intense bouncing (1-2 hours) High-impact sports: Basketball, volleyball, gymnastics - sports with lots of jumping For Avoiders: No bouncing: Avoid all bouncing and jumping activities Feet-on-ground activities: All activities keep feet planted on ground Slow movements: Any movement slow and controlled, no fast/bouncy motion Low-impact exercise: Walking, swimming (not diving), gentle bike riding Massage Techniques: Calf massage: Deep massage of calf muscles (work hard during bouncing), 3-5 minutes per leg Foot and ankle massage: Massage entire foot and around ankle joint, 3 minutes each foot
Achilles tendon attention: Gentle massage along Achilles tendon (connects calf to heel), 1-2 minutes per leg Shin massage: Massage front of lower leg (shins), 2 minutes per leg Vestibular Integration: Heavy landings: Encourage landing with flat feet, heavy impact (not just toe bouncing) for more proprioceptive input Jump and hold: Jump up, land in squat and hold for 5 seconds - combines vestibular with proprioceptive Bilateral integration: Jump while clapping, catching ball, or doing arm movements - integrates whole body Manifestation 2: Jumping Up and Down in Place (10-100 consecutive jumps) Physical Redirect Technique: Join the child jumping for 10 jumps, then say "Great jumping! Now let's count how high we can jump." Do 10 controlled jumps focusing on maximum height, counting together. Then say "Time for strong stillness" - have them stand still, feet planted, push down into ground, hold 20 seconds. Alternate: 10 high jumps / 20 seconds stillness / repeat 3 times.
DIY Alternative Tool: Structured Jumping System: Jump counter app: Use free counter app, child tracks jumps, set daily goals and limits Jump spot with target: Mark a spot on floor with tape, hang paper from ceiling - child jumps to touch target (purposeful jumping) Jumping intervals timer: Use interval timer - 30 seconds jumping / 60 seconds rest / repeat 10 times Jump height chart: Mark wall with tape lines at different heights, child tries to jump to touch higher lines Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Jumping games: Jump over tape lines on floor, jump over pillow obstacles, "hot lava" jumping from spot to spot Squat jumps: Deep squat, explosive jump up, land in squat - more intense input with fewer jumps needed
Long jumps: Instead of vertical jumping, long jumps across room (measures progress) Stair jumping: Jump up to first or second stair (safe surface), provides upward jumping challenge Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Jump rope routine: 5-10 minutes jump rope 2-3x daily, structured jumping activity Trampoline with variations: Jump on trampoline doing different movements (tuck jumps, star jumps, twist jumps) Jumping games: Hopscotch, jump the river, Simon Says jumping, musical statues with jumping Plyometric exercises: Box jumps, burpees, jump squats (if age appropriate) - high-intensity jumping For Avoiders: No jumping: Eliminate jumping requirements Stepping instead: Step up onto low step instead of jumping Supported landing: If must jump, land on very soft surface (thick mat, sand) Arm movements only: Do arm exercises (arm raises, circles) instead of jumping
Massage Techniques: Full leg massage: Massage entire leg from hip to ankle focusing on muscles used in jumping, 5 minutes per leg Knee support massage: Massage around knee joint (not directly on it), 2 minutes each knee Hip flexor massage: Massage front of hip (hip flexors work hard in jumping), 3 minutes each side Lower back massage: Jumping impacts lower back, massage thoroughly, 5 minutes Vestibular Integration: Jump with direction changes: Jump forward, backward, side-to-side, turning - varies vestibular input Eyes closed jumping: Brief eyes-closed jumping (with spotter) challenges vestibular system more Rhythmic jumping: Jump to music beat, to metronome, or counting - adds organization to jumping Manifestation 3: Bouncing on Furniture (Beds, Couches) for 20-60+ minutes Physical Redirect Technique: Approach bouncing child, place hand near them and say firmly but calmly "Furniture is for sitting. Bouncing goes here instead." Immediately guide them to safe bouncing location (trampoline, cushion pile on floor, or outside on grass). Have them bounce there for 5-10 minutes, then set timer for next bouncing session (30-60 minutes later).
DIY Alternative Tool: Safe Bouncing Alternative: Floor cushion bounce pit: Stack 6-8 couch cushions on floor in designated area, this becomes "legal" bouncing spot Mattress on floor: Place old mattress or crib mattress on floor in playroom/basement - designated bouncing surface Air mattress: Partially inflate air mattress, place on floor, safe bouncing surface Furniture vs. trampoline rule chart: Visual chart showing red X on furniture, green check on trampoline - clear rule display Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Mini trampoline indoors: 3-4 foot trampoline in designated room provides safe indoor bouncing Outdoor trampoline: If space/budget allows, large outdoor trampoline provides maximum bouncing opportunity Pogo stick: If old enough (age 5+), pogo stick provides intense bouncing Hop ball: Large inflatable ball with handle child sits on and bounces, directs bouncing urge
Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Scheduled furniture bouncing: Allow furniture bouncing at specific times with rules (10 minutes after school on old couch in basement) Trampoline routine: 15-20 minute trampoline sessions 3-4x daily with specific exercises (tuck jumps, seat drops, front flips if skilled) Bouncing transitions: Use quick bouncing session (2-3 minutes) before transitions (before homework, before meals) to regulate Bounce-based play: Games on trampoline (trampoline basketball, trampoline Simon Says, bounce counting contests) For Avoiders: No bouncing anywhere: Avoid all bouncing activities Stable furniture only: Very stable, heavy furniture that doesn't move Ground-based activities: All play and movement stays on stable ground Seated activities: Prefer sitting activities with no bouncing component Massage Techniques: Post-bouncing full body massage: After bouncing sessions, 10-15 minute full body massage to organize nervous system
Joint compressions: Compress all major joints (ankles, knees, hips) after bouncing, 10 seconds each - adds proprioceptive input Deep pressure massage: Very firm pressure massage focusing on legs, back, core muscles used in bouncing Calming conclusion: End with slow, rhythmic strokes and deep breathing to transition from high activity Vestibular Integration: Bouncing with tasks: While bouncing, do tasks (catch ball, count, answer questions) - integrates vestibular with other skills Gradual intensity reduction: Start session with wild bouncing, gradually reduce height/intensity, end with gentle bouncing then stillness Eyes open/closed: Practice bouncing eyes closed briefly (safely) to challenge vestibular system differently Manifestation 4: Trampolining for Hours Physical Redirect Technique: Approach trampoline, stand at edge and call child's name. When they stop, say "You've been jumping for X minutes. Time for a bounce break." Have them step off trampoline, do 10 wall push-ups and 10 squats, drink water, walk around 2-3 minutes. Then may return for another timed session (15-20 minutes maximum per session).
DIY Alternative Tool: Trampoline Management System: Trampoline timer: Use large timer visible from trampoline, set for 20-minute sessions, must exit when timer sounds Trampoline chart: Track trampoline time on chart - max 60-90 minutes total per day broken into sessions Activity rotation: Trampoline 15 min → different activity 15 min → trampoline 15 min (prevents hours of continuous jumping) Trampoline games with breaks: Structured games requiring breaks (jump 50 times, break, do tricks, break, bounce game, break) Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Trampoline alternatives: If don't have trampoline - jumping on grass, cushion pile jumping, stair step-ups repeated Varied trampoline activities: Change activities on trampoline - bounce games, trying tricks, exercise routines, not just bouncing Water breaks mandatory: Every 15 minutes, must exit trampoline for water and 3-minute break
Intensity variation: Alternate high-intensity bouncing with low-intensity gentle bouncing Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Structured trampoline routine: Create specific routine - 5 min warm-up bouncing, 10 min tricks/games, 5 min cool-down bouncing, repeat max 3x daily Trampoline park enrollment: Weekly 1-2 hour sessions at trampoline park as main vestibular outlet Gymnastics class: Enroll in gymnastics providing structured trampoline time with instruction Other vestibular activities: Rotate between trampoline and other vestibular inputs (swinging, spinning, climbing) to vary input For Avoiders: No trampoline: Avoid trampolines entirely Stable alternatives: Activities on stable ground only Gentle rebounders: If any bouncing, only gentle rebounders (very small movement) Watching others: May prefer watching others on trampoline rather than participating Massage Techniques: Post-trampoline recovery massage: 15-20 minute massage after long trampoline sessions focusing on legs, back, core
Foam rolling: Use foam roller on legs after trampolining, 5 minutes, reduces muscle soreness Calf and foot focus: Extra attention to calves and feet which absorb impact, 5 minutes Cold therapy: If overused, ice massage on calves and feet 5 minutes reduces inflammation Vestibular Integration: Trampoline boundaries training: Practice stopping on command on trampoline - builds self-regulation Skill development: Work on specific trampoline skills/tricks - makes time purposeful not just seeking Integration activities: Follow trampoline with activities integrating vestibular input (drawing, writing, calm reading) - helps organize nervous system Manifestation 5: Hopping Instead of Walking Physical Redirect Technique: When child is hopping, call their name and walk toward them. Say "Time for walking feet" and demonstrate exaggerated walking steps. Hold their hand and walk together for 20-30 steps counting aloud. Say "Great walking! Hopping is for recess/outside time." Redirect to walking every time you notice hopping in inappropriate contexts.
DIY Alternative Tool: Hopping vs. Walking Management: Visual cue cards: Make two cards - HOPPING (green, picture of hopping) and WALKING (red, picture of walking). Show appropriate card for each situation Hop spot: Designate specific area (masking tape square on floor) where hopping is allowed, rest of house requires walking Hop counter: Count daily hops with goal of reducing (start at 200 hops per day, reduce weekly) Hopscotch path: Create hopscotch path where hopping is appropriate, emphasizes hopping has specific place/time Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Scheduled hopping time: 5-10 minute hopping sessions 3x daily in designated area, satisfies urge Hopping games: Structured hopping activities (hop races, hop to targets, hopping obstacle courses) Galloping/skipping: Alternative movement patterns (galloping, skipping) provide similar input but look more typical
Animal walks: Bear crawl, crab walk, bunny hops as games/exercises rather than transportation Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Hopping exercises: 50 hops on right foot, 50 on left, 50 on both - structured hopping workout 2x daily Hopscotch: Create elaborate hopscotch patterns, play regularly Jumping rope: Provides similar input in more socially acceptable form Sports with hopping: Activities like jumping rope games, certain dances, hopscotch tournaments For Avoiders: Walking only: No hopping, jumping, or bouncing Smooth, even gait: Focus on smooth, controlled walking Avoid uneven surfaces: Stay on smooth, flat surfaces for walking Hand-holding: Hold hand or rail when walking for security Massage Techniques: Single leg massage: Extra massage for hopping leg if child hops on one leg more, 5 minutes
Bilateral leg massage: Equal massage both legs even if hopping symmetrically, 5 minutes each Hip and knee joint attention: Massage around hip and knee joints stressed by hopping, 3 minutes each Balance and alignment massage: Massage with focus on encouraging balanced muscle use Vestibular Integration: Walk-hop intervals: Practice walking 10 steps, hopping 10, walking 10 - builds ability to transition Slow motion hopping: Slow, controlled hops requiring more balance and control Hopping with tasks: Hop while carrying item, catching ball - integrates hopping with function Manifestation 6: Knee Bouncing While Seated (Constant, Throughout Day) Physical Redirect Technique: Sit beside child, place hand gently on their bouncing knee and say "Let's give your knee a rest." Guide them to plant both feet flat on floor, press down firmly, hold for 10 seconds. Then allow 20 controlled knee bounces. Then press down again. Alternate: 10 sec still / 20 bounces / 10 sec still.
DIY Alternative Tool: Seated Bouncing Alternatives: Foot fidget box: Place box under desk with textured items, tennis ball, bubble wrap - feet fidget instead of knees bouncing Resistance band on chair: Tie resistance band between front chair legs, push feet against band instead of bouncing knees Wobble cushion: Sit on partially inflated cushion, allows whole body movement instead of just knee Theraband around chair legs: Loop theraband around chair legs at knee height, push knees out against resistance Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Foot roller under desk: Tennis ball, water bottle, or foot roller under desk to roll feet on Stress ball: Hold/squeeze stress ball in hands during seated activities Gum chewing: Rhythmic chewing may reduce bouncing urge Music with headphones: Rhythmic music provides auditory rhythm replacing physical bouncing
Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Pre-sitting movement: Before seated activities, 5 minutes vigorous movement (jumping jacks, running in place, squats) Seated movement breaks: Every 15-20 minutes, stand and do 10 jumping jacks, sit back down Active sitting options: Therapy ball as chair, wobble cushion, standing desk option Leg exercises at desk: Lift legs one at a time, hold 10 seconds, 10 reps each leg For Avoiders: Very stable seating: Solid, heavy chair that doesn't move Feet well-supported: Proper footrest so feet are planted and supported Back support: High-backed chair with armrests for full body support Short sitting periods: Limit sitting time to 15-20 minutes before movement break Massage Techniques: Leg massage before sitting: Before seated activities, massage legs 5 minutes to reduce fidgeting
Under-desk hand massage: Quick 2-minute hand massage during seated tasks (self-applied or by adult) Knee area massage: Massage around knee joint and thigh muscles, 3 minutes each leg Evening leg massage: Thorough leg massage at end of day, 10 minutes, releases tension from bouncing Vestibular Integration: Proprioceptive instead of vestibular: During sitting, focus on proprioceptive input (weighted lap pad, feet pressure, hand fidgets) Visual anchoring: Focus eyes on work/screen reduces movement need Bilateral coordination: Use both hands for tasks, engages both brain sides reducing fidgeting Manifestation 7: Bouncing on Exercise Balls for Extended Periods Physical Redirect Technique: Approach child on ball, place hand on their shoulder and say "Time to check in. How long have you been bouncing?" Set timer for remaining session (15 minutes maximum from time you check). When timer sounds, child must dismount, do 10 wall push-ups, drink water, different activity for 10 minutes minimum before returning to ball.
DIY Alternative Tool: Exercise Ball Management: Ball timer system: Timer attached to ball area, set for 15-minute sessions, visual/audio cue when time ends Ball chart: Track ball time daily, max 60 minutes total split into 15-minute sessions Ball alternatives rotation: Ball 15 min → wobble cushion on chair 15 min → regular chair 15 min → repeat Activity on ball: Structure activities to do on ball (watch 1 TV show, read 1 chapter, complete 1 worksheet) instead of just bouncing Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Peanut ball: Oval-shaped exercise ball - more stable than round, allows bouncing with less rolling risk Wobble cushion on chair: Partially inflated cushion on regular chair provides movement without full ball instability Therapy ball games: Games on ball - bounce and catch, balance challenges, roll on stomach over ball - purposeful use
Ball exercises: Structured exercises on ball (bridges, planks with feet on ball, sit-ups) instead of just bouncing Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Structured ball routine: 15 min morning (bouncing warm-up), 15 min afternoon (ball exercises), 15 min evening (calm bouncing) Ball as chair: Use ball as chair for homework/activities allowing movement during functional tasks Ball sports: Engage in activities using large balls (exercise ball soccer, rolling races, ball tossing games) Variety in bouncing: Change position on ball (sitting, kneeling, lying over), vary bounce intensity For Avoiders: No ball sitting: Avoid exercise balls entirely Stable seating: Very stable chairs only Feet on ground: All sitting positions with feet firmly on ground Observe only: May watch others use ball without participating Massage Techniques:
Post-ball core massage: Massage back and abdominal muscles (core works hard on ball), 5-10 minutes Hip flexor massage: Sitting on ball tightens hip flexors, massage front of hips, 3 minutes each Lower back attention: Ball sitting can strain lower back, thorough lower back massage, 5 minutes Glute massage: Gluteal muscles work for balance on ball, massage thoroughly, 3 minutes each side Vestibular Integration: Ball with reduced bounce: Partially deflate ball reducing bounce while maintaining instability Bilateral activities on ball: While bouncing, do bilateral tasks (pat knees alternately, arm movements) - integrates hemispheres Progressive stability: Start with stable chair, advance to wobble cushion, then therapy ball - gradual vestibular challenge Manifestation 8: Jump-Landing Repeatedly (Seeking Impact Sensation) Physical Redirect Technique: When observing intense jump-landing behavior, approach and say "I see you need strong landing feelings. Let's do landing practice properly." Guide through 10 jump-landings with focus: jump up, land with bent knees (absorbing impact), hold squat 3 seconds, repeat. Count together. Then transition to different proprioceptive activity (wall push-ups, heavy carrying).
DIY Alternative Tool: Impact Landing Station: Crash mat: Stack 6-8 couch cushions or use old mattress on floor - safe impact landing zone Sand landing pit: If outdoor space, dig shallow pit, fill with sand (12 inches deep) - natural impact absorber Jump-and-land targets: Mark landing spots with tape, child jumps from designated height to target spots - structured landing practice Landing counter: Count landings per session, set limits (50 landings per session, 3 sessions daily) Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Stair jumping: Jump down from bottom 2-3 stairs onto thick mat or cushion (supervised) Box jumps: Use sturdy box or step, jump up, step down carefully (up jumping preferred), repeat Depth jumps: Jump off low surface (stair, curb) landing in squat position - controlled impact
Stomp dancing: Heavy stomping movements to music provide impact sensation Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Scheduled impact sessions: 10 minutes 3x daily of structured jumping/landing activities Trampoline to ground: Jump on trampoline then jump off onto mat - intense impact sensation Heavy landing exercises: Jump squats, burpees, plyometric exercises - legitimate heavy landings Crash pad games: Run and jump into crash pad, do different landing positions (superhero, cannonball) For Avoiders: No jumping/landing: Avoid all impact activities Soft, gentle movements: Only slow, controlled movements Stable surfaces: Activities on very stable, cushioned surfaces Gradual exposure: If must participate, very short duration, lots of support Massage Techniques: Heel and foot massage: Impact stress feet heavily, deep foot massage, 3-5 minutes each Calf deep tissue: Calves absorb landing impact, deep massage up and down calf muscles, 5 minutes each
Knee support massage: Massage all around knee joint (not on it), 3 minutes each knee Full leg compression: Firm compression massage from hip to ankle after impact activities, 5 minutes each leg Vestibular Integration: Landing practice: Teach proper landing technique (bent knees, land mid-foot not toes, absorb impact) - protects joints Impact with proprioceptive focus: Emphasize the "feeling" of landing in body, increasing body awareness Varied heights: Practice landing from different heights, different surfaces - varies vestibular challenge
Comprehensive Stimming Guide > 5. VESTIBULAR STIMMING > A. Linear Movement Stimming > Level 3: Swinging
Causation: Over-stimulated: Smooth, rhythmic swinging is deeply calming Under-stimulated: Intense vestibular input from movement and gravity changes Sensitivity: Vestibular-seeking; craves sensation of movement through space Emotional Regulation: Swinging releases calming neurochemicals Gravitational Security: Learning to trust body in space Sensory Profile: Seeker: Fast, high swinging; seeks intense vestibular input Linear Seeker: Prefers back-forth over rotational; may become nauseous with spinning Calming Seeker: Slow, gentle swinging for self-soothing Description: Pendular or rotational movement while suspended Manifestation 1: Swinging on Playground Swings for 30-120+ Minutes Physical Redirect Technique: Approach swing set, stand where child can see you and call their name. When they slow enough to hear, say "You've been swinging for X minutes. Let's take a swing break." Help them dismount safely, immediately do 10 jump squats and walk around playground once. Sit for 2-3 minutes drinking water. May return for another 15-20 minute swing session after break.
DIY Alternative Tool: Swing Time Management: Swing timer: Use sports timer or phone timer visible from swing, set for 20-minute sessions Swing tracker chart: Log swing time on chart, set daily maximum (60-90 minutes total), child monitors own time Activity rotation: Swing 15 min → different playground equipment 10 min → swing 15 min Token system: Child gets 3 swing tokens daily, each token = 20 minutes swing time, when tokens gone, swinging done for day Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Indoor swing: Install swing in doorway or ceiling beam (heavy-duty), allows swinging at home in controlled amounts Hammock: Outdoor or indoor hammock provides similar input to swinging Rocking chair: Substitute some swing time with rocking chair time Therapy swing: Indoor platform or net swing (occupational therapy equipment) for home use
Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Varied swinging: Change swing types during session (belt swing, tire swing, disc swing, platform swing) - varies input Swinging with activity: While swinging, do activities (catch ball, reach for objects, answer questions) - integrates vestibular with other skills Amplitude variation: Practice swinging high, medium, low - different intensities throughout session Direction variation: Swing forward-back, twist for rotational, side-to-side if possible For Avoiders: No swinging: Avoid swings entirely Stable playground equipment: Use slides, climbing structures with feet always connected to surface Observe others: May enjoy watching others swing from safe distance Gentle alternatives: If any movement, very gentle rocking chair only Massage Techniques: Post-swinging grounding massage: 10-15 minutes full body massage after long swinging sessions to help nervous system integrate input
Back and core focus: Swinging uses back and core muscles, massage thoroughly, 7-10 minutes Neck and shoulders: Holding onto swing chains strains neck/shoulders, massage these areas, 5 minutes Vestibular calming massage: Massage base of skull (sub-occipital region) which houses vestibular centers, 3-5 minutes Vestibular Integration: Eyes open vs. closed: Practice brief periods swinging with eyes closed (safely) - intensifies vestibular challenge Stop and start: Practice stopping swing, holding still, restarting - builds vestibular self-regulation Post-swing activities: Follow swinging with organizing activities (drawing, puzzles, reading) - helps integrate vestibular input Manifestation 2: Seeking Maximum Swing Height and Speed Physical Redirect Technique: Stand at safe distance from swing, when child is at highest point, call out "Level check!" Child reports their swing "level" (1-10 scale, 10 being highest). Say "Let's try level 5" (medium height). Coach them to reduce amplitude gradually by dragging feet slightly. When at level 5 for 10 swings, say "Perfect safe swinging!" Practice various levels building awareness and control.
DIY Alternative Tool: Swing Height Management: Visual height markers: Tie colored ribbons at different heights on swing set poles (green=safe, yellow=careful, red=too high) Spotter system: Adult or peer stands at safe distance, signals when height is appropriate or too high Self-regulation training: Teach child to self-monitor by feeling sensations - "safe swinging feels ___" vs. "too high feels ___" Swing arc measurer: Use chalk or tape to mark maximum safe swing arc on ground Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Controlled swinging challenges: "Can you swing exactly this high for 20 swings?" (set safe height), "Can you swing smoothly without jerky movements?" Different swing types: Tire swing, disc swing, net swing provide intense input at lower heights Double swinging: Two people on swing together reduces maximum achievable height
Weighted vest swinging: Wear weighted vest while swinging, increases intensity at lower heights Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Intensity through duration: Swing at moderate height for longer rather than extreme height briefly Platform swing: Large platform swing allowing lying down - feels more intense than sitting swing Double-platform swinging: Adult and child swing together on platform swing - very intense without excessive height Indoor vestibular alternatives: When extreme swinging urge hits, redirect to spinning on office chair, somersaults, rolling For Avoiders: No high swinging: Avoid all swinging, especially high amplitude Feet-touching swings: If any swinging, low enough for feet to touch ground throughout Minimal movement: Only gentlest, shortest arc swinging if required to participate Alternative activities: Suggest climbing, sliding, or other playground activities instead
Massage Techniques: Deep pressure grounding: After intense swinging, very firm pressure massage all over body, 15 minutes - helps organize overstimulated nervous system Joint compressions: Compress all major joints for 10 seconds each after swinging - adds proprioceptive organization Slow rhythmic strokes: Very slow, heavy pressure strokes down body - calming and organizing Vestibular integration massage: Massage sub-occipital area, behind ears, along jaw - targets vestibular system Vestibular Integration: Gradual intensity reduction: Start session with desired height/speed, gradually reduce over 10-15 minutes before stopping Stopping practice: Practice coming to complete stop from high swinging - builds self-regulation skills Varied planes: Some sessions forward-back, some sessions with twisting/rotational - varies vestibular challenge Manifestation 3: Twisting Swing Chains and Spinning Physical Redirect Technique: Approach twisted swing before child sits, place hands on chains and say "I see you want spinning. Let's do twist-spins safely." Help child sit, twist chains for them (controlled amount - 10-15 twists), check they're ready, release for spin. Count spins together. After spin stops, wait 30 seconds for system to recover, repeat only 3-5 times per session.
DIY Alternative Tool: Twist-Spin Management: Twist counter: Mark starting point on chain with colored tape, count number of twists before releasing (set safe maximum of 15-20 twists) Rotation timer: Between spins, must wait 60 seconds for vestibular system recovery (use timer) Twist-spin tokens: 5 tokens per playground visit, each token = one twist-spin, teaches moderation Direction alternation rule: Must alternate spinning direction (clockwise, then counterclockwise) - reduces dizziness, builds bilateral vestibular function Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Office chair spinning: Swivel office chair allows controlled spinning at home Sit-and-spin toy: Even beyond typical age, provides safe spinning opportunity Merry-go-round: Playground merry-go-round provides rotational input (supervised, moderate speed) Rolling down hills: Substitute spinning with rolling sideways down hills - rotational vestibular input Sensory Integration Activities:
For Seekers: Structured twist-spin routine: 5 twist-spins, 5 minutes break, 5 more twist-spins, done (prevents excessive spinning) Spin variations: Vary number of twists (5, 10, 15), spin direction, sitting vs. standing on swing Indoor spinning: Office chair spins, spinning in place, somersaults - provides rotational input without swing access Bilateral spinning: Same number of spins in each direction every session - builds balanced vestibular system For Avoiders: No spinning: Avoid all rotational movement Linear swinging only: If any swinging, only forward-back, no twisting Visual stability: Keep eyes focused on one stable point if near spinning activities Exit strategy: If accidentally exposed to spinning, immediate exit and grounding activities Massage Techniques: Post-spinning stabilization massage: 10-15 minutes massage emphasizing slow, rhythmic, grounding strokes
Neck and shoulder release: Spinning creates neck/shoulder tension, massage thoroughly, 5-7 minutes Sub-occipital massage: Gentle pressure at base of skull where vestibular processing occurs, 3-5 minutes Bilateral symmetrical massage: Massage both sides of body simultaneously, supports bilateral vestibular integration Vestibular Integration: Recovery time enforced: Always 45-60 seconds minimum between spins for nervous system recovery Reduced spinning over time: Goal is gradually decreasing number/intensity of spins as vestibular system matures Post-spin organizing activities: After spinning session, quiet activities (reading, puzzles) help organize vestibular input Manifestation 4: Hanging from Bars While Swaying Physical Redirect Technique: Stand below hanging child, place hand near their leg and say "Let's count your strong hang time." Count to 20 seconds, then say "Time to dismount safely." Help if needed. Have them do 10 squats and shake out arms. Then may hang again for 20 seconds. Pattern: 20 sec hang / movement break / 20 sec hang / repeat 3-5 times only per session.
DIY Alternative Tool: Hanging-Swaying Management: Hang timer: Use smartphone timer visible from bar, set for 20-30 second hangs with mandatory breaks Hang counter: Track number of hangs daily (max 15-20 hangs per day), child self-monitors Alternating activities: Hang/sway 30 sec → monkey bars crossing → hang/sway 30 sec → swing → repeat circuit Progressive challenge: Week 1: 15-second hangs, Week 2: 20-second hangs, Week 3: 25-second hangs - builds gradually Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Indoor pull-up bar: Over-door pull-up bar allows controlled hanging at home (always supervised, crash mat below) Tree branch hanging: Sturdy low tree branch provides natural hanging opportunity Monkey bars routine: Instead of static hanging, move across monkey bars - functional hanging activity Doorway hang: Brief hangs from stable doorframe (if appropriate weight and door is solid)
Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Varied hanging positions: Arms straight, bent elbows, one hand, hanging from knees (if equipment allows) - varies proprioceptive input Hanging with swaying: Intentional controlled swaying while hanging - combines proprioceptive and vestibular Hanging games: Hang and play games (20 questions, I Spy) - makes hanging purposeful Upper body strength circuit: Integrate hanging into circuit with push-ups, pull-ups, climbing - comprehensive proprioceptive input For Avoiders: No hanging: Avoid all hanging activities Supported positions: If must be on bars, sitting on bar or holding while feet on ground Brief touches only: Just touch bar, no weight-bearing hanging Alternative upper body: Wall push-ups, light weights seated - avoid hanging/inverting Massage Techniques: Shoulder decompression: After hanging, massage shoulders while gently pulling arms to decompress joints, 5 minutes
Forearm and hand massage: Hanging stresses these areas intensely, deep massage, 5 minutes Upper back and lats: Hanging uses latissimus dorsi muscles heavily, massage thoroughly, 5-7 minutes Wrist attention: Massage wrists and do gentle rotations to release tension from hanging grip Vestibular Integration: Swaying vs. static: Alternate between swaying while hanging and staying still - different vestibular challenges Visual focus: While hanging and swaying, practice focusing eyes on one point - integrates visual-vestibular Controlled dismount: Always practice controlled, safe dismounting - body awareness and planning Manifestation 5: Seeking Hammocks, Hanging Chairs, or Suspended Seats Physical Redirect Technique: When child has been in hammock/hanging chair for extended period, approach and say "Time for a hanging break. Your body needs movement variety." Help them exit, immediately do 10 jumping jacks and walk around area 2-3 minutes. May return for another 15-20 minute session.
DIY Alternative Tool: Suspended Seating Management: Indoor hammock: Install hammock in child's room or playroom for controlled access DIY hanging chair: Use sturdy fabric and rope to create simple hanging seat from ceiling beam or tree Time limits posted: Sign near hammock stating "Maximum 20 minutes per session, 2 breaks between sessions" Activity requirement: May use hammock only while doing activity (reading, listening to music, not just rocking) Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Rocking chair alternative: When hammock unavailable, rocking chair provides similar rhythmic movement Therapy swing indoors: Platform swing or net swing hung in doorway or from ceiling Blanket hammock: Drape strong blanket over sturdy furniture creating makeshift hammock (supervised) Bean bag chair: Deep bean bag chair provides cocooning feeling similar to hammock
Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Hammock routine: 15 min morning, 20 min afternoon, 20 min evening - structured hammock time Active hammock use: While in hammock, do activities (read, craft, listen to stories) - purposeful hanging time Varied suspension: Rotate between hammock, hanging chair, regular swing - different types of suspended feeling Hammock exercises: Sit-ups in hammock, rolling side to side, rocking variations - active use For Avoiders: No suspended seating: Avoid hammocks, hanging chairs, swings Stable seating: Only solid, grounded furniture Recliner alternative: If seeking cocooning feeling, use stable recliner instead Ground-based nests: Create cozy reading nook on floor with pillows instead of suspended options Massage Techniques: Post-hammock grounding: After hammock time, firm pressure massage focusing on grounding, 10 minutes
Back and hip massage: Hammock positioning can strain back/hips, massage thoroughly, 7-10 minutes Neck and shoulder release: Suspended positions often create neck tension, massage 5 minutes Full body linear strokes: Long strokes from head to toe, grounding and organizing, 5-10 minutes Vestibular Integration: Gradual stillness: End hammock sessions with gradually reducing rocking until still before exiting Proprioceptive transition: After hammock, immediate proprioceptive activities (push-ups, carrying heavy items) helps organize system Visual calming: Dim environment around hammock reduces visual stimulation, allows focus on vestibular input Manifestation 6: Rocking Chairs with Intense, Sustained Rocking Physical Redirect Technique: Sit in chair nearby, establish eye contact and say "Let's rock together calmly." Model slow, controlled rocking at 60 BPM (use metronome app). Rock together for 5 minutes, then say "Time for stillness" - both stop completely, breathe deeply 3 times, then slow walk around room together. Child may return to rocking chair but with timer set for 15 minutes.
DIY Alternative Tool: Rocking Chair Management: Metronome pairing: Keep metronome app near rocking chair, set to 60-80 BPM, child rocks to beat (prevents excessive speed) Rocking chart: Track rocking time daily, set maximum (60 minutes total per day in multiple sessions) Activity-based rocking: May rock while reading, listening to music, doing craft - purposeful rocking Rocking chair timer: Visual timer on table next to chair, set for 15-20 minute sessions Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Multiple rocking options: Have rocking chair in 2-3 locations (bedroom, living room, playroom) so always accessible appropriately Glider rocker: Glider-style rocker provides smoother, more controlled movement than traditional rocker Therapy ball: When rocking chair unavailable, sitting on therapy ball provides similar movement opportunity Porch swing: Outdoor porch swing provides rocking alternative with fresh air
Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Structured rocking routine: 15 min morning (wake-up rocking), 15 min after school (transition), 20 min before bed (wind-down) Rocking with reading: Assign specific books/reading time to rocking chair, makes rocking productive Varied rocking: Change speed and amplitude during session - fast rocking 5 min, slow rocking 10 min Family rocking time: Parent and child each in rocking chairs talking together - social + sensory For Avoiders: Stable seating only: Avoid rocking chairs entirely Heavy, non-moving furniture: Use only solid furniture that doesn't rock or move Grounded positions: All seating with feet firmly on floor Minimal movement: Avoid any furniture with movement capability Massage Techniques: During rocking massage: Provide massage while child continues gentle rocking (back massage while they rock)
Post-rocking calming: After intense rocking, 10-15 minute full body massage to organize nervous system Lower back focus: Rocking can strain lower back, thorough massage of lumbar region, 5 minutes Foot grounding massage: Massage feet thoroughly after rocking to help "ground" child, 3 minutes each foot Vestibular Integration: Speed variation training: Practice rocking at different speeds - helps develop vestibular modulation Eyes open vs. closed: Alternate rocking with eyes open and closed (briefly) - different vestibular challenge Bilateral activities while rocking: While rocking, do hand activities (pat knees alternately, clapping patterns) - integrates both sides of brain Manifestation 7: Creating Makeshift Swings from Ropes, Sheets, etc. Physical Redirect Technique: When you discover child creating makeshift swing, approach calmly and say "I see you need swinging. Let's find the safe swing." Remove makeshift swing explaining safety concerns. Immediately take child to approved swing (playground, indoor therapy swing, or create approved safe swing together). If no swing available, substitute with rocking chair or therapy ball for immediate vestibular input.
DIY Alternative Tool: Safe Swing Creation: Approved DIY swing: Work together to create safe swing - thick rope, board seat, secure to proper beam (adult installs/supervises), this becomes "our special swing" Indoor therapy swing: Purchase indoor swing kit (platform, disc, or net swing) properly installed in doorway or from ceiling beam Tree swing: Create proper tree swing with adult supervision - thick rope, stable branch, proper height Swing safety rules poster: Create poster together showing safe vs. unsafe swinging, hang near any swings Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Hammock installation: Properly install hammock providing similar suspended feeling safely Blanket swing game: Two adults hold corners of sturdy blanket, child sits in middle for gentle swinging (brief, supervised) Resistance band pull: Loop resistance band, child sits in center while adult pulls sides creating rocking motion
Playground visits: Schedule regular playground trips (daily if possible) for safe swinging access Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Swing access provided: Recognize intense swinging need, provide appropriate safe swinging options at home and plan playground visits Swing substitutes: When swinging unavailable, immediate substitutes (rocking chair, therapy ball bouncing, spinning on office chair) Vestibular diet: Comprehensive vestibular sensory diet including multiple activities (spinning, swinging, rolling, jumping) Problem-solving together: Work with child to identify safe ways to meet swinging needs For Avoiders: Remove swinging temptations: No swings or hanging items in environment Stable alternatives: Provide appealing stable activities (building, crafts, reading nooks) Ground-based movement: If needs movement, walking, running, dancing on stable ground Safety emphasis: Explain that avoiding swinging is about safety and comfort
Massage Techniques: Creativity redirection massage: After stopping unsafe swing attempt, provide 10-minute calming massage redirecting energy Full body proprioceptive input: Deep pressure massage all muscle groups, 15 minutes, satisfies sensory need safely Organizing massage: Slow, rhythmic massage that organizes nervous system, 10 minutes Vestibular calming massage: Focus on base of skull, neck, shoulders, 5-7 minutes Vestibular Integration: Understanding the need: Recognize makeshift swing creation indicates intense unmet vestibular need Appropriate outlets: Provide multiple appropriate vestibular outlets preventing unsafe seeking Supervised creativity: Channel creativity into safe swing creation projects with adult help Manifestation 8: Swinging from Tree Branches or Climbing Structures Physical Redirect Technique: If child is swinging from unsafe branch/structure, calmly say "That branch isn't safe. Let's find a better swinging spot." Help them down safely, immediately redirect to safe swinging option. If no better option available, that moment is not swinging time - offer alternative vestibular input (spinning, jumping on trampoline, running). Work together to identify approved safe trees/structures for future swinging.
DIY Alternative Tool: Safe Swinging Structure Identification: Approved branch markers: Identify safe, strong tree branches together, mark with colored tape, "green tape branches are safe for swinging" Structure safety check: Assess climbing structures together, identify which parts safe for swinging/hanging, mark clearly Weight limit signs: Post weight limits on various structures, teach child to assess safety Alternative location map: Create map of home/neighborhood showing all safe swinging locations Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Proper tree swing installation: Work with adult to properly install swing on approved strong branch with appropriate equipment Playground structure use: Use playground climbing structures as intended (climbing, not swinging from unsafe parts) Adult-supervised climbing: Climbing activities with adult spotting providing safety Indoor climbing wall: If feasible, install small indoor climbing wall with proper mats (alternative to risky outdoor climbing)
Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Approved climbing/swinging routine: Daily time (30-45 minutes) on approved structures with supervision Climbing class: Enroll in rock climbing class providing safe climbing/hanging opportunities with instruction Supervised free play: Outdoor play time with adult supervision allowing adventurous play safely Risk assessment skills: Teach child to assess structure safety (shake branch, check stability, weight limits) For Avoiders: Ground-based activities: All activities on stable ground Low structures only: If any climbing, only low structures with feet near ground Adult proximity: Adult close by for reassurance during any height-related activities Alternative adventures: Nature walks, animal watching, ground-level exploration Massage Techniques: Post-climbing recovery: After climbing/swinging sessions, full body massage focusing on arms, shoulders, legs, 15 minutes Hand and forearm massage: Climbing/swinging stresses hands/forearms, deep massage, 5-7 minutes
Shoulder decompression: After hanging from branches, massage shoulders and gently decompress, 5 minutes Leg and core massage: Climbing uses legs and core intensely, massage thoroughly, 10 minutes Vestibular Integration: Height and movement combination: Swinging from height combines vestibular with proprioceptive and visual input (very intense) Gradual exposure: Start with low branches/structures, gradually increase height as skills improve Safety skills integration: Teach how to test branch strength, proper grip, safe dismounting - builds body awareness and planning
Comprehensive Stimming Guide > 5. VESTIBULAR STIMMING > B. Rotational Movement Stimming > Level 1: Spinning While Standing
Causation: Over-stimulated: Intense vestibular input can paradoxically organize nervous system Under-stimulated: Craves powerful rotational vestibular stimulation Sensitivity: Vestibular system under-responsive; needs intense input to register Visual + Vestibular: Enjoys combined sensation of movement + blurred vision Endorphin Release: Dizziness may trigger neurochemical reward Sensory Profile: Extreme Seeker: Spins until dizzy; immediate spinning after recovery; hours daily Rotational Preference: Specifically seeks spinning over linear movement Bilateral: May prefer spinning in one direction over the other Description: Rotating body around vertical axis Manifestation 1: Spinning in Circles (10-100+ Consecutive Spins) Physical Redirect Technique: As child is spinning, say loudly enough to hear "Spin check!" Child stops spinning (if too dizzy to stop safely, let them finish naturally and sit down). Say "You've done X spins. Let's do 5 more spins together slowly, then stop." Do 5 slow, controlled spins together counting aloud. Then have them sit immediately, feet flat on floor, hands on knees, breathe deeply for 60 seconds to let vestibular system recover.
DIY Alternative Tool: Spin Control System: Spin counter app: Use free counter app, child clicks after each spin (builds awareness), set daily limit Spin spot: Mark a specific spot on floor with tape, spinning only allowed on this spot (contains activity) Rotation timer: Set timer for 2-3 minutes, spinning allowed only while timer runs, then mandatory 5-minute rest Direction alternation rule: Must alternate spin direction (5 spins right, rest, 5 spins left, rest) - builds bilateral vestibular and reduces dizziness Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Office chair spinning: Sit in swivel office chair, spin in controlled manner (adult controls speed if needed) Sit-and-spin toy: Even beyond typical age, provides controlled spinning opportunity Lazy Susan spinning: Child sits on large lazy Susan (carefully), adult spins slowly
Hula hoop spinning: Spin hula hoop on arm or around body instead of spinning self Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Structured spin sessions: 10 spins, 2-minute rest, 10 spins, 2-minute rest, 10 spins, done (3x daily) Spin variations: Spin with arms out, arms in, on one foot, on toes - provides variety Bilateral spinning protocol: Same number spins each direction every session - must do 10 right, then 10 left Post-spin activities: After spinning, organizing activities (building, puzzles, drawing) - helps integrate vestibular input For Avoiders: No spinning: Avoid all rotational activities Linear movement only: Forward-back movement only (swinging, rocking), no rotation Stable visual field: Keep environment still, avoid watching others spin Grounding activities: Activities that keep body oriented and stable
Massage Techniques: Post-spinning grounding massage: Immediately after spinning, 10-minute firm pressure massage focusing on grounding Bilateral symmetrical massage: Massage both arms together, both legs together - reinforces bilateral integration Vestibular calming massage: Massage base of skull (sub-occipital area), behind ears, along jaw - directly affects vestibular system Long axis strokes: Massage in long strokes from head to toe following body's length - very organizing after rotational input Vestibular Integration: Recovery time mandatory: 90-120 seconds between spin bouts for vestibular system recovery Eyes open vs. closed: Practice brief spinning with eyes closed (very carefully) - intensifies vestibular challenge Reducing spin count: Goal is gradually reducing number of spins as vestibular system matures Manifestation 2: Twirling While Walking Physical Redirect Technique: When child is twirling while walking, catch up and walk alongside them. Say "Let's practice walking in a straight line." Hold their hand if they accept it, walk together in straight line counting steps for 20 steps. Then say "Now you try alone" and watch them walk straight for 20 more steps. Praise straight walking. If twirling resumes, repeat.
DIY Alternative Tool: Walking Management: Floor path: Use colored tape to create walking path on floor, child follows path (makes straight walking visual) Twirl zones: Designate specific areas where twirling allowed (marked with tape), rest of house requires straight walking Twirl allowance: Allow twirling every 50 straight steps - child counts steps, gets twirl break, continues Walking helper: Use walking stick or holding onto furniture edges while walking - tactile guide for straight walking Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Scheduled twirl time: Specific times/locations for twirling (after school 5 minutes in yard, before bed 3 minutes in room) Twirling games: Structured twirling activities (ballet/dance routines, twirling ribbon wands, spin-and-freeze game) Balance beam walking: Walk on tape line or 2x4 board on floor - requires focus, prevents twirling
Heavy item carrying: While walking, carry heavy item (books, laundry basket) - prevents twirling, adds proprioceptive input Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Dance/ballet class: Structured twirling within dance routines - purposeful, appropriate twirling Twirling toys: Twirl ribbon wands, batons, hula hoops instead of self Skating/rollerblading: Activities allowing spinning/twirling movements appropriately Vestibular substitutes: When can't twirl, substitute with other vestibular input (swinging, rocking, jumping) For Avoiders: Straight line focus: Practice only straight-line walking, no rotations Hand-holding: Hold hand or push shopping cart while walking for stability Visual focus: Focus eyes on destination point while walking Slow, deliberate steps: Very controlled, careful walking Massage Techniques: Leg and hip massage: Twirling uses leg and hip muscles intensely, massage thoroughly, 5-7 minutes each leg Core strengthening massage: Massage abdominal and back muscles supporting twirling, 5 minutes
Balance integration massage: Massage while child stands on one foot (alternating) - challenges balance during massage Foot reflexology: Deep foot massage, grounding after twirling activity, 3 minutes each foot Vestibular Integration: Controlled twirls: Practice twirling specific number of times (3 twirls), stopping cleanly, walking straight - builds control Bilateral practice: Equal twirls both directions - right turns and left turns balanced Environmental awareness: While walking straight, practice noticing environment - integrates vision with vestibular Manifestation 3: Pirouettes or Dancer-Like Spinning Physical Redirect Technique: When child is doing pirouettes, approach and say "Beautiful spinning! Let's count perfect pirouettes." Have them do 5 slow, controlled, proper-form pirouettes (spot the head, balanced landing) with you counting. Then say "Excellent! Now let's rest your spinning system" - have them stand still, feet together, arms at sides, breathe deeply for 60 seconds.
DIY Alternative Tool: Dance Spin Management: Pirouette counter: Track proper pirouettes per day (set limit of 50-100), encourages quality over quantity Dance routine structure: Create short dance routines including pirouettes (routine = 3 pirouettes, other moves, 2 pirouettes, other moves) - embeds spinning in broader activity Mirror practice: Practice pirouettes in front of mirror - increases body awareness and control Spot marker: Put sticker on wall at eye level, practice "spotting" (keeping eyes on sticker while turning) - proper dance technique reduces dizziness Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Dance video routines: Follow online dance videos including spins/turns - structured dancing Music-based spinning: Only spin while music plays, when music stops must stop - external control Pirouette variations: Practice different types of turns (chaine turns, pique turns) - provides variety
Performance routine: Create performance routine for family including spins - makes spinning purposeful Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Ballet/dance class enrollment: Structured class teaching proper technique satisfies spinning need appropriately Daily dance practice: 20-30 minute practice sessions including stretching, turns, jumps - comprehensive activity Dance games: Just Dance video game, dance freeze, musical statues - spinning within games Rhythmic gymnastics: Sport combining dance, flexibility, apparatus work including lots of turning For Avoiders: No spinning/turning: Avoid all rotational dance movements Linear dance movements: Only forward-back, side-to-side dancing, no turns Seated movement: Movement activities while seated (no standing/spinning required) Slow, grounded movement: Tai chi, slow yoga - controlled, stable movement Massage Techniques: Ankle and foot massage: Pirouettes stress ankles and feet, thorough massage, 5 minutes each foot
Calf and thigh massage: Leg muscles work hard for pirouettes, deep massage, 5 minutes each leg Core massage: Ballet/dance requires strong core, massage abdominal and back muscles, 7-10 minutes Neck and shoulder release: Spotting technique and arm positions can create neck/shoulder tension, massage 5 minutes Vestibular Integration: Spotting technique: Teach proper spotting (head stays facing forward as long as possible, then whips around) - reduces dizziness, improves technique Single vs. multiple turns: Practice single clean pirouette, then double, then triple - progressive challenge Both directions: Equal practice both directions (right and left turns) - bilateral vestibular development Manifestation 4: Spinning Until Dizzy, Then Repeating After Recovery Physical Redirect Technique: Observe child spinning to dizziness and recovering. After recovery phase, approach and say "I notice you spin until dizzy. Let's try spinning that stops before dizzy." Guide them through 10 controlled spins at moderate speed, stop before dizzy. Say "Notice your body feels alert but not dizzy - that's the goal." Practice "stop before dizzy" spinning, gradually building awareness of body signals.
DIY Alternative Tool: Dizziness Prevention System: Body awareness training: Teach child to rate dizziness 1-10, practice stopping at level 5-6 before reaching 8-10 Spin counter with limit: Use counter, stop at predetermined number (15 spins) before dizziness hits Timer approach: Spin for 30 seconds only (usually prevents dizziness), rest, repeat Adult monitoring: Adult watches, signals child to stop when observe signs of approaching dizziness (wobbling, off-balance) Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Controlled spinning alternatives: Office chair spinning (adult controls speed), slow lazy Susan spinning, gentle merry-go-round Post-spin recovery spot: Designated comfortable spot to sit/lie during recovery phase (bean bag chair, couch corner with pillows) Visual anchoring after spin: After spinning, immediately focus on one stable object for 30 seconds - speeds recovery
Water ritual: After spinning, drink cold water slowly - helps reset nervous system Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers (High Tolerance Group): Gradual tolerance building: Work toward tolerating more vestibular input without dizziness (proper technique, conditioning) Varied rotational activities: Distribute rotational input across multiple activities (office chair spinning, rolling, somersaults, pirouettes) instead of one extreme spinning session Proprioceptive loading post-spin: After spinning, immediate heavy work (push-ups, carrying, wall pushes) helps organize dizzy feelings Ice activities: Roller skating, ice skating provide rotational input with speed limits For Avoiders: No spinning to dizziness: Avoid all activities causing dizziness Minimal rotation: If any spinning, 2-3 slow rotations maximum Immediate stop: If any dizziness sensation, stop activity immediately Recovery priority: Focus on activities that never create dizziness
Massage Techniques: Emergency grounding massage: If child spinning to problematic dizziness, immediate firm pressure massage to help ground, 5-10 minutes Vestibular reset massage: Sub-occipital massage (base of skull), behind ears, neck - targets vestibular system, 5 minutes Bilateral symmetrical strokes: Massage both sides of body simultaneously, supports vestibular integration Slow, rhythmic whole-body massage: Very slow strokes from head to toe, 10-15 minutes, deeply organizing Vestibular Integration: Habituation principle: Repeated controlled exposure to rotational movement (not to dizziness!) can gradually improve vestibular tolerance Recovery time respect: Always allow full recovery before additional spinning - typically 2-3 minutes minimum Understanding the seeking: Dizziness may release endorphins; need to find healthier ways to achieve similar calming/rewarding feelings Manifestation 5: Spinning in Both Directions Alternately
Physical Redirect Technique: Observe child's bilateral spinning pattern. Approach and say "I notice you spin both ways - that's actually really good for your brain! Let's do it with counting." Guide them through 10 spins clockwise (counting together), 60-second rest, 10 spins counterclockwise (counting together), done. Praise the bilateral pattern while adding structure. DIY Alternative Tool: Bilateral Spinning Structure: Direction cue cards: Make two cards - RED (spin right/clockwise) and BLUE (spin left/counterclockwise). Place cards in rotation, child follows sequence Even count tracker: Chart tracking spins each direction, goal is keeping them equal (10 right = 10 left each session) Bilateral spinner toy: Fidget spinner or top that child spins with fingers - tactile bilateral activity replacing body spinning Metronome with alternation: Spin right for 30 seconds (metronome at 60 BPM), rest, spin left for 30 seconds
Alternative Stimulation (Household Items): Bilateral activities substitution: When spinning urge hits, do other bilateral activities (cross-crawls, march with opposite hand/knee touches, figure-8 arm movements) Spinning objects: Spin objects bilaterally (top in right hand, then left hand; spin ball on finger right hand, then left) Rolling variations: Roll right down hill, walk back up, roll left down hill - same vestibular system use Twisting games: Twister game, yoga twists both directions, turning head side-to-side exercises Sensory Integration Activities: For Seekers: Bilateral vestibular routine: Structured routine always including equal input both sides (10 right spins, 10 left spins, 5 right rolls, 5 left rolls) Cross-lateral movements: Activities crossing body midline (tennis, swimming, cross-country skiing) - integrates both brain hemispheres Bilateral sports: Sports requiring bilateral rotation (tennis, golf, baseball) - functional rotational training
Mirror practice: Practice skills on both sides (kick ball with right foot, then left; throw with right hand, then left) For Avoiders: No bilateral rotation: Avoid rotational movements entirely Minimal head turning: Limit even head turning side-to-side Forward-facing activities: All activities facing forward, minimal rotation required Supported environment: Stable, predictable environment with minimal rotation demands Massage Techniques: Bilateral massage technique: Always massage both sides of body equally (right arm, then left arm with same strokes/pressure/duration) Cross-pattern massage: Massage right arm while having child lift left leg (and vice versa) - cross-lateral integration Spinal rotation massage: Gentle spinal twists (with massage) each direction - bilateral trunk rotation Symmetry focus: Massage ensuring perfect symmetry bilaterally supports bilateral vestibular integration Vestibular Integration: Bilateral integration goal: Spinning both directions is actually therapeutic and integrative - want to maintain this pattern while adding control
Hemispheric balance: Bilateral rotation supports both brain hemispheres working together Functional benefit: This spinning pattern is healthier than unilateral spinning only - support and structure it rather than eliminate Manifestation 6: Spinning While Watching Hands/Environment Blur Physical Redirect Technique: As child is spinning watching hands blur, say "Pause!" Have them stop spinning and stand still. Say "Let's watch your hands while standing still instead."
